# Receipt Image Resize & Zoom Design **Date:** 2026-08-03 **Status:** ✅ Built (pending release) — gate moved after resize with a 25MB decode guard, 2400px @ 85%, HEIC/PNG transcoded to JPEG, zoom ceiling derived per image, `/admin/resize-images` deleted. The two [open questions](#open-questions) below are still open. Resize-on-upload and zoom both already ship (`901b670`). This is a correction to both, driven by a real failure: a phone photo was refused with "Image too large. Max 5MB." by the line immediately before the one that would have shrunk it to ~400KB. The governing decision — the size limit describes the **Receipt Image** we store, not the **Source File** we are handed — is recorded in [ADR-0006](../adr/0006-the-stored-image-is-the-contract.md), with the vocabulary and invariants in [the domain model](../domain-model.md). This document is the implementation shape. ## The defect ``` uploadAndCreate() ReceiptService.ts:186 ├─ validateFile(file) :187 ← rejects Source File > 5MB └─ withRetry( :190 prepareFileForUpload() :191 ← resize to 2000px / 85% uploadToStorage() :192 ``` `validateFile` (`:164`) reads `file.size` on the picked file. `MAX_IMAGE_MB = 5` (`:13`) is small next to a modern phone photo — 3–5MB typically, 8–12MB at 48MP — so the gate fires on files the pipeline exists to shrink. Nothing downstream rescues it. `FileValidator` (`src/lib/server/fileValidation.ts:13`, 10MB, magic-number based) is server-side and not on this path. The email-ingestion path (`supabase/functions/resend/handler.ts:137`) has no size check at all, so the same receipt forwarded by email is accepted at full size while the upload button refuses it. ## Changes ### 1. Validation splits in two `validateFile` currently answers one question with three checks. It becomes two gates around the resize: **Before decode** — file type against the allow-list, plus a **25MB** ceiling on any type. This ceiling is a memory guard, not a policy about receipts: it stops a 200MP panorama or a RAW export from hanging the tab before Canvas is even reached. Comfortably above a 48MP iPhone photo and a multi-page scanned PDF. **After resize** — the existing `MAX_IMAGE_MB` (5) / `MAX_PDF_MB` (10) applied to the file actually being uploaded. Note the shift in what a rejection _means_. `prepareFileForUpload` swallows any resize error and returns the original (`:215`), so a 12MB photo whose resize fails — Canvas OOM, a corrupt EXIF block, HEIC on a non-Apple browser — now falls back to a 12MB original that the second gate refuses. The file is refused either way, but the reason is "we could not shrink this", and the message must say that rather than repeating "too large", which would send the person off to do something that will not help. ### 2. Resize accepts HEIC and PNG, and always emits JPEG `resizeImage` returns early for anything that is not JPEG or PNG (`imageResize.ts:72`), while the upload control offers `image/heic` (`src/routes/receipts/+page.svelte:492`). Two independent problems follow from the format handling: - **HEIC is skipped entirely** — the backlog has flagged this as unverified on-device since the mobile-capture PRD. Safari (macOS/iOS) can decode HEIC into Canvas and Chrome/Firefox cannot, which is fortunate: HEIC only originates on Apple platforms. Feed it through the same path and fall back to the untouched original elsewhere. - **PNG is never compressed.** `canvas.toBlob(cb, file.type, quality)` (`:104`) ignores the quality argument for lossless formats, so 85% has never applied to a PNG. There is also no keep-the-smaller-file guard, so a sub-threshold PNG is re-encoded at identical dimensions and returned even when the result is bigger than what the person picked. Screenshots of e-receipts are usually PNG. Both dissolve if the output is always JPEG. `toBlob` is called with `'image/jpeg'` regardless of input, and the storage path extension follows. `original_filename` is unaffected and must stay that way — it deliberately captures the pre-resize name (`#{#ofn2a}`, `ReceiptService.ts:283`) so a receipt is listed under the name its owner recognizes, even though the stored object is now `.jpg`. **Consequential fix:** `extractReceiptDataFailSoft(path, file.type)` (`:193`) passes the _original_ file's MIME type while the object at `path` is the resized one. Harmless today; a live bug the moment HEIC transcodes, because OCR would be told `image/heic` about a JPEG. It must take the uploaded file's type. ### 3. Pixel budget: 2400px longest axis at 85% Up from 2000px, for headroom on receipts photographed at a distance, where the receipt occupies a fraction of the frame. Expected stored size ~500–800KB. The comment at `imageResize.ts:58` ("Images smaller than 2000px still have compression applied") is false for PNG today and should be corrected rather than carried forward. ### 4. Zoom stops at native resolution `ReceiptImageViewer.svelte` fits the image to the viewport at 100% (`handleImageLoad`, `:72`) and caps at a flat `MAX_ZOOM = 400` (`:56`). Those two constants were chosen independently and disagree: a 2400×1000 receipt on a 1440px-tall laptop fits at ~1150px, so 100% is ~48% of native and 400% asks the browser to paint ~4800px from a 2400px file. Everything past roughly 210% is interpolation. On a phone the same 400% lands near 1:1, so the current constant is approximately right there and badly wrong on a desktop. `MAX_ZOOM` becomes derived: `100 × naturalWidth / baseWidth`, the zoom at which one image pixel occupies one CSS pixel. `ZOOM_STEP` is 50 and `zoomIn`/`zoomOut` snap to multiples of it (`:127`, `:134`), so the derived ceiling will rarely be a multiple of 50 — the top step must clamp to the ceiling rather than skip past or become unreachable. Where the fit scale is already clamped at 1 (`:78`) — any image at or below viewport size — the ceiling equals `MIN_ZOOM` and both buttons sit permanently disabled. That is the accepted outcome, not an edge case to patch: there are no further real pixels, and the disabled control says so. It affects small PNGs and low-resolution receipts uploaded before resizing existed. ### 5. Delete `/admin/resize-images` A one-off migration page (~260 lines) whose job is finished. It would now do active harm — it re-resizes at its own hardcoded constants, permanently destroying the extra detail in pre-`901b670` full-resolution originals that the native-resolution zoom ceiling is designed to exploit. It is also the unauthenticated delete-and-reupload route recorded as **M2** in the [backlog](../product-backlog.md); deleting it closes the finding outright. Removing it also removes the second caller of `resizeImage`, so the new constants have exactly one call site. ### No backfill Storage will hold three generations of Receipt Image — full-resolution from before `901b670`, 2000px since, 2400px after this change. A ceiling derived from each image's own dimensions handles all three correctly with no migration; the older full-resolution receipts simply permit more zoom. ## What is deliberately not changing - **The email path.** `handler.ts:137` uploads attachment bytes straight to storage, unresized and ungated. It is a Deno edge function with no Canvas, so matching this behaviour means a WASM image library plus a second copy of the resize rules in `supabase/functions/_shared/`, kept in lock-step by hand — the same maintenance burden CLAUDE.md already flags for the date-correction code, and CPU time inside a webhook that must answer quickly. Logged as a backlog item instead. - **PDFs.** Stored as received, gated at 10MB, no zoom in the viewer (`isPdf`, delegated to the browser's PDF renderer). ## One deviation from the design as agreed The design said resize would stay inside `withRetry`, re-decoding on each attempt — wasteful but harmless. Moving validation after the resize changed that calculus: a size rejection thrown inside `withRetry` would be retried three times with backoff, so the person waits ~2.8 seconds per file for a verdict that could not change. Both the resize and the artifact check now sit **outside** the retry, which leaves the network steps (upload → OCR → insert) as the only retried work and incidentally removes the repeated decode. Nothing that was retried before has stopped being retried. ## Memory `resizeImage` decodes the file twice: it builds an `` from an object URL purely to get an `onload` (`:77`, `:152`), then ignores that element and decodes the same bytes again via `createImageBitmap(file)` (`:89`). Peak memory is doubled on exactly the large files the 25MB ceiling now admits, and on an older phone that is the difference between working and a crashed tab. The `` is removable — `createImageBitmap` is itself the decode and needs no prior load event. This is a correctness prerequisite for raising the ceiling, not a tidy-up. In its favour: `processUploadBatch` (`src/lib/utils/batchUpload.ts:44`) is a sequential `for…of await`, so a multi-file selection never holds more than one decode at a time. ## Testing - `imageResize.spec.ts` (node) — dimension maths at the new 2400px threshold, the accepted-type list, the JPEG renaming rule, and that HEIC reaches `createImageBitmap` with `imageOrientation: 'from-image'` rather than being skipped. - `imageResize.svelte.spec.ts` (**browser**) — the function's body. The `.svelte.spec.ts` suffix is the only route into the Chromium project; in node `createImageBitmap` and `document` are both undefined, so without this file `resizeImage` never actually executes anywhere and transcoding is unverified. Asserts on the produced file: JPEG type and `.jpg` name, longest axis capped at 2400px with the ratio preserved, a photo shrinking by more than half, and a transparent PNG landing on **white** rather than black. - `ReceiptService.uploadValidation.spec.ts` — a Source File over 5MB but under 25MB now succeeds (the reported failure, as a regression test); over 25MB is refused before `resizeImage` is called at all; a transcoded file over 5MB is still refused; a resize failure on a large file is refused with the shrink-failure message and on a small one falls back to the original, stored under its own extension and content type; the transcode lands under a `.jpg` key; the MIME sent to OCR matches what storage received. - `ReceiptImageViewer.svelte.spec.ts` — ceiling derived from natural size (the image is never painted wider than `naturalWidth`); controls disabled when natural ≤ viewport; the clip box matches `VIEWPORT_FRACTION`. - Manual, on-device: an iPhone upload end-to-end, plus the gesture check already standing in the backlog (wheel/drag/pinch after the a11y action refactor). Note the browser project is advisory only — Vercel's `buildCommand` runs `vitest run --project server` ([ADR-0005](../adr/0005-quality-gate-in-the-vercel-build-not-github-actions.md)), so the transcode and zoom-ceiling tests gate nothing. That is the standing trade-off, not something specific to this change. ## Known limits, deliberately left - **The fit is computed once, at image load.** `baseWidth`/`baseHeight` come from the window size at the moment the receipt decodes, and nothing recomputes them on resize, so after resizing the window the receipt no longer fills the intended fraction. The 1:1 ceiling stays exact regardless (it is derived from the same `baseWidth` used to scale), so the "never invents pixels" invariant holds — only the fit goes stale. Pre-existing behaviour, unchanged here. - **`MAX_SOURCE_MB` guards bytes, but decode cost is driven by pixels.** A well-compressed 3MB 12000×9000 scan still allocates ~430MB of RGBA. The same exposure existed under the old 5MB cap, five times smaller; a pixel-count guard would need the dimensions, which are only known after the decode starts. ## Open questions 1. **Does 2400px buy OCR anything?** Mistral's vision model downscales large inputs internally; if its effective ceiling is ~1024–1500px on an axis, the extra pixels serve human zoom only. Worth confirming against Mistral's docs — it does not change the decision, but it changes the rationale, and it would let a future storage squeeze cut resolution without touching OCR accuracy. 2. **What does an iPhone actually hand over?** Still unverified on-device. The transcode is designed to work whether Safari offers HEIC or converts to JPEG itself, so this is validation rather than a blocker.

## claude.ai Dropbox
# Claude App MCP LLM Boot Instructions

You are the assistant for Dropbox's Claude App MCP server. Your goal is to help users complete Dropbox tasks quickly and correctly while minimizing friction.

## Customer Use Cases

This app is best at helping users do these Dropbox workflows:

- Browse folder contents and paginate through large directories.
- Find files quickly using plain-language search terms and then open files with follow-on tools.
- Inspect file metadata (size, type, timestamps, IDs, sharing context).
- Check signed-in Dropbox identity, team/account context, and namespace-root context.
- Read text content from supported files up to 5 MiB, and provide a usable Dropbox link even when text extraction fails.
- Generate single-use temporary download links when the user explicitly needs direct file download URLs.
- Generate file previews with thumbnail and "open in Dropbox" experiences.
- Create folders in the right destination before saving artifacts.
- Create new text files directly in Dropbox.
- Create share links for files/folders and return the effective sharing settings.
- Inspect and list existing shared links.
- List, inspect, and create Dropbox file requests.
- Move, rename, copy, and delete Dropbox files/folders after explicit confirmation.
- Check the status of long-running move, copy, and delete jobs.

When users ask "what can you do?", summarize these use cases in plain language before taking action.

## Not Supported (Do Not Advertise)

- Editing or overwriting existing file content in place.
- Saving URL-hosted files directly into Dropbox.
- Uploading local/binary artifacts via `upload_file`.
- Permanent file deletion or wipe workflows. `delete` moves items to the user's Dropbox "Deleted files" area only.
- Reliable text extraction for supported files via `fetch`; extraction may still fail for some files, in which case the tool error may include a usable link.
- E-signature initiation or signing workflows.
- Actions outside Dropbox content management and sharing.

## devonthink
CRITICAL — Database package safety: DEVONthink databases are stored as packages (.dtBase2) or sparse images (.dtSparse, .dtArchive). Never modify, rename, move, or delete files inside a database package directly via the filesystem. All record and content operations must go through this MCP server or, as a fallback, via AppleScript. Direct filesystem manipulation will corrupt the database and cause irreversible data loss.

Batch operations: Use the uuids array parameter instead of sequential single-record calls for tag, update, move, trash, duplicate, replicate, and export operations. Batch mode is faster, reduces round trips, and returns a summary with succeeded/failed counts.

Avoiding duplicates: Use lookup_records (by name, URL, path, filename, or comment) before create_record to check whether a record already exists.

Content editing: Prefer update_record_content with mode append or insert over replace for large documents. Replace mode requires sending the entire new content and risks accidental data loss if the content is incomplete.

Group hierarchies: Use create_group_path to create nested group structures in a single call (like mkdir -p) rather than sequential create_record calls.

AI-powered tools: classify_record and find_similar_records use DEVONthink's built-in AI algorithms and proprietary training data — they provide organizational suggestions that complement, not duplicate, your own capabilities.

Record enrichment: resolve_doi_metadata and resolve_book_metadata can enrich existing records with bibliographic metadata by passing the record's uuid — there is no need to create a new record.

AI exclusion: Records marked as excluded from AI access (excludeFromChat) are protected in two ways. (1) Input protection: any tool that receives such a record's UUID as an argument refuses to operate on it and returns an error. (2) Output protection: result lists from tools like search_records, classify_record, find_similar_records, get_record_children, get_record_duplicates, and the link traversal tools are filt… [truncated]

## omnifocus
OmniFocus is a GTD task manager. Hierarchy: Folders > Projects > Tasks > Subtasks.

TASK STATES: Available, Blocked, Deferred (future defer date), Flagged, Overdue, Completed, Dropped. Planned Date is a scheduling signal only — no availability/overdue constraints.

PROJECT TYPES: "sequential" (tasks in order; first incomplete = available, rest blocked; position = dependencies), "parallel" (all available), "single_actions" (no completion goal, cannot auto-complete). The `next` field is true for the first available action in a sequential project/action group; in parallel projects, all incomplete tasks have `next: true`.

ACTION GROUPS: Task with subtasks. Parent shows `blocked: true` while subtasks are active — this is normal, not an error. Do not try to unblock it.

INHERITED STATUS: `completed`/`dropped` reflect the task's own state, not its container's. `effectivelyCompleted`/`effectivelyDropped` reflect the container's state — if true, the task's parent project or action group was completed/dropped. Task in completed project: `completed: false`, `effectivelyCompleted: true`, `available: false`. Use `available_only=True` for actionable tasks.

EFFECTIVE DATES: Dates returned by get_tasks are always effective (inherited). A task with no direct due date WILL show its project's due date in the dueDate field — this is correct behavior, not a bug. You cannot clear an inherited date at the task level. Write operations set the task's own date.

RECURRING TASKS: `completed=True` uses `mark complete`, which creates the next occurrence. This is guaranteed. WARNING: Dropping a recurring task (status='dropped') without clearing recurrence first (recurrence='') spawns the next occurrence. To stop a series: update_tasks([{"id": "...", "recurrence": "", "status": "dropped"}]).

TAGS: Represent work contexts. Tag statuses: Active (normal), On Hold (tasks excluded from Available perspective), Dropped (tag hidden from picker; does NOT affect task availability).

DEFER vs DUE: Defer = hidden until that date. Due = deadline.

docs/product-backlog.md:21:- **iPhone camera / mobile capture.** Use the camera on an iPhone to take photos of receipts. Designed in [PRD — Mobile Capture](prd-mobile-capture.md): a single-purpose, chrome-free `/capture` route installed to the home screen as a PWA (`start_url: /capture`, `display: standalone`) — **not** a native iOS app, since the camera and photo library already work in mobile Safari and what's missing is a phone-shaped surface, not a capability. Reuses `ReceiptService.uploadAndCreate()` behind a queued, immediately-re-arming shutter. Requires a route-group split of `src/routes/+layout.svelte` (auth gate out, nav chrome into `(app)`). That worked only because fit-to-box guaranteed the image always fitted at 100%; now that a tall receipt overflows at 100%, native scrolling is blocked and the manual handler declines to engage. Recorded as an accepted asymmetry in [ADR-0006](adr/0006-the-stored-image-is-the-contract.md) and the ["Every uploaded image becomes JPEG" invariant](domain-model.md). Revisit if storage cost or emailed-receipt volume grows.

# Fit-to-width, and no pixel ceiling for vector receipts

Amends the scope of
[ADR-0006](0006-the-stored-image-is-the-contract.md). That decision's raster
reasoning stands; this one says what it is about.

## Context & decision

ADR-0006 settled two things about the viewer: 100% means fit-to-viewport, and
zoom stops at the image's own natural resolution. Both were written about a
photograph. An emailed receipt is not one — `renderTextToSvg` typesets the email
body into an SVG — and both rules fail on it.

**A vector image has no pixel ceiling.** `calculateMaxZoom` stops where one image
pixel fills one CSS pixel, which for a resolution-independent format is a
category error: there is no pixel grid to exhaust. On the reported receipt it
computed to ~128%, which is the "even after you click zoom it barely grows"
symptom exactly. Vector images get a flat **800%** ceiling instead — arbitrary,
finite only so the zoom-in button can honestly disable itself and a stray gesture
cannot ask the browser to lay out a 40,000px element.

**100% becomes fit-to-width**, `scale = min(viewportWidth / naturalWidth, 1)`,
for **all** images. Fitting the whole image inside 90vw × 80vh means the height
binds for any tall document, so a 1100 × 2000 SVG landed ~530px wide and its own
`font-size` cancelled out. This is not an SVG problem — a photo of a long CVS
receipt failed identically.

Neither breaks the "zoom never invents pixels" invariant. Fit-to-width still caps
`scale` at 1, so nothing is ever painted past native; and an SVG has no pixels to
invent. The invariant is a statement about raster images, and a
resolution-independent format falls outside it.

## Considered options

  images. Rejected: an arbitrary constant would need defending forever, and a

5	# The stored image is the contract
6	
7	> **Scope amended by
8	> [ADR-0007](0007-fit-to-width-and-a-vector-zoom-ceiling.md).** Everything below
9	> is about _raster_ receipts. 100% is now fit-to-_width_, and an emailed receipt
10	> — an SVG — has no pixel ceiling to stop at.
11	
12	## Context & decision
13	
14	`ReceiptService.uploadAndCreate()` validated the file the person picked and
15	_then_ shrank it. The 5MB limit therefore measured the **Source File** while the
16	resize that would have made it ~400KB ran on the next line.
17	
18	The fix is to decide what the limit is _about_. **The limit describes the
19	artifact we keep, not the artifact we are handed.** Size validation moves after
20	the resize, so it gates the **Receipt Image**; the Source File is bounded only by
21	a 25MB pre-decode ceiling that exists to protect the browser's memory, not to
22	judge the receipt. Everything follows from that principle:
23	
24	- **2400px longest axis at 85% JPEG.** The stored image is what a person zooms
25	  into, so the pixel budget is chosen for human reading, not for OCR.
26	- **HEIC and PNG transcode to JPEG.** One stored format. PNG additionally never
27	  honoured the 85% quality argument (`toBlob` ignores it for lossless formats),
28	  so a PNG "resize" could return a file _larger_ than it arrived.
29	- **Zoom stops at the image's own natural resolution**, replacing a flat
30	  `MAX_ZOOM = 400`. 100% is fit-to-viewport, so a fixed percentage meant
31	  different things per device: on a phone 400% was roughly 1:1, on a desktop it
32	  demanded ~2.3× more detail than a 2000px file contains. The mush people saw at
33	  high zoom was the viewer promising pixels the resize had already discarded.
34	- **No backfill.** A per-image ceiling reads each generation correctly on its
35	  own. Re-resizing the pre-`901b670` full-resolution originals would destroy
36	  detail we already paid to store — so `/admin/resize-images` is deleted rather
37	  than updated, which also closes the **M2** finding (an unauthenticated
38	  delete-and-reupload page) instead of deferring it a fourth time.
39	
40	## Considered options
41	
42	- **Raise `MAX_IMAGE_MB` from 5 to ~15.** A one-line unblock, rejected because
43	  the gate would still measure the wrong artifact: a 16MB photo that resizes to
44	  400KB is still refused for no reason the family can perceive.
45	- **Keep the gate, improve the error message.** Cheapest, and the honest reading
46	  of it is "we have automated shrinking, and we are going to ask you to do it
47	  anyway."
48	- **Keep PNG lossless, add a keep-the-smaller-file guard.** Genuinely defensible
49	  — JPEG ringing around small glyphs is real, and screenshot receipts have sharp
50	  edges. Rejected for a single stored format; at 2400px and 85% the artefacts are
51	  well below the threshold that matters for reading a total.
52	- **Two artifacts per receipt** — a small display/OCR copy plus a large read
53	  copy. Best quality-per-byte, rejected as doubling the storage objects and
54	  adding a second signed-URL path to every surface that shows a receipt.
55	- **Cap zoom at ~1.5× native** rather than a hard 1:1, keeping some headroom
56	  because magnification past 1:1 still helps low-vision readers even though it
57	  adds no information. Rejected in favour of the stricter rule: every pixel on
58	  screen is a real pixel.
59	
60	## Consequences
61	
62	- **Transcoding is irreversible and lossy.** Detail discarded at upload never
63	  comes back — there is no original to re-derive from, by design. Revisiting the
64	  2400px/85% numbers only affects receipts uploaded after the change.
65	- **A PNG screenshot can come out _larger_ than it arrived.** JPEG spends bits on
66	  the hard edges of rendered text that PNG encodes almost for free, so for a
67	  sharp-edged e-receipt screenshot already within the pixel budget the transcode
68	  can grow the file. Measured, not theoretical. This is the cost of the single
69	  stored format and is accepted; the keep-the-smaller-file guard above is the
70	  alternative if it ever matters. Photographs — the overwhelming majority —
71	  shrink by well over half.
72	- **JPEG has no alpha, so the canvas must be painted white first.** A
73	  transparent-background PNG composites onto _black_ by default (the HTML spec
74	  requires it), which would store dark text on a black field as the only copy of
75	  the receipt.
76	- **Zoom disappears for small images.** Anything already at or below viewport
77	  size has `MIN_ZOOM == MAX_ZOOM` and both controls sit disabled. Accepted
78	  deliberately over faking magnification.
79	- **A resize failure now becomes a rejection.** `prepareFileForUpload` falls back
80	  to the original on any error; a 12MB original then fails the post-resize gate.
81	  The file is refused either way, but the real reason is "we could not shrink
82	  it", and the message must say so rather than blaming the file's size.
83	- **The email path diverges.** The Resend handler uploads attachment bytes
84	  straight to storage with no size check and no resize (Deno — no Canvas), so an
85	  emailed receipt is stored full-size while the same receipt uploaded in the
86	  browser becomes 2400px JPEG. Resizing there needs a WASM image library and a
87	  second copy of these rules in `supabase/functions/_shared/`, kept in lock-step
88	  by hand. Logged in the [backlog](../product-backlog.md) rather than built.
89	- **Storage now holds three generations** of Receipt Image and always will. This
90	  is fine for zoom (see the "Zoom never invents pixels" invariant) but means
91	  storage-size statistics are not comparable across upload dates.

- **Raise `MAX_IMAGE_MB` from 5 to ~15.** A one-line unblock, rejected because
  the gate would still measure the wrong artifact: a 16MB photo that resizes to
  400KB is still refused for no reason the family can perceive.
- **Keep the gate, improve the error message.** Cheapest, and the honest reading
  of it is "we have automated shrinking, and we are going to ask you to do it
  anyway."
- **Keep PNG lossless, add a keep-the-smaller-file guard.** Genuinely defensible
  — JPEG ringing around small glyphs is real, and screenshot receipts have sharp
  edges. Rejected for a single stored format; at 2400px and 85% the artefacts are
  well below the threshold that matters for reading a total.
- **Two artifacts per receipt** — a small display/OCR copy plus a large read
  copy. Best quality-per-byte, rejected as doubling the storage objects and
  adding a second signed-URL path to every surface that shows a receipt.
- **Cap zoom at ~1.5× native** rather than a hard 1:1, keeping some headroom
  because magnification past 1:1 still helps low-vision readers even though it
  adds no information. Rejected in favour of the stricter rule: every pixel on
  screen is a real pixel.

## Consequences

- **Transcoding is irreversible and lossy.** Detail discarded at upload never
  comes back — there is no original to re-derive from, by design. Revisiting the
  2400px/85% numbers only affects receipts uploaded after the change.
- **A PNG screenshot can come out _larger_ than it arrived.** JPEG spends bits on
  the hard edges of rendered text that PNG encodes almost for free, so for a
  sharp-edged e-receipt screenshot already within the pixel budget the transcode
  can grow the file. Measured, not theoretical. This is the cost of the single
  stored format and is accepted; the keep-the-smaller-file guard above is the
  alternative if it ever matters. Photographs — the overwhelming majority —
  shrink by well over half.
- **JPEG has no alpha, so the canvas must be painted white first.** A
  transparent-background PNG composites onto _black_ by default (the HTML spec
  requires it), which would store dark text on a black field as the only copy of
  the receipt.
- **Zoom disappears for small images.** Anything already at or below viewport
  size has `MIN_ZOOM == MAX_ZOOM` and both controls sit disabled. Accepted
  deliberately over faking magnification.
- **A resize failure now becomes a rejection.** `prepareFileForUpload` falls back
  to the original on any error; a 12MB original then fails the post-resize gate.
  The file is refused either way, but the real reason is "we could not shrink
  it", and the message must say so rather than blaming the file's size.
- **The email path diverges.** The Resend handler uploads attachment bytes
  straight to storage with no size check and no resize (Deno — no Canvas), so an
  emailed receipt is stored full-size while the same receipt uploaded in the
  browser becomes 2400px JPEG. Resizing there needs a WASM image library and a
  second copy of these rules in `supabase/functions/_shared/`, kept in lock-step
  by hand. Logged in the [backlog](../product-backlog.md) rather than built.
- **Storage now holds three generations** of Receipt Image and always will. This
  is fine for zoom (see the "Zoom never invents pixels" invariant) but means
  storage-size statistics are not comparable across upload dates.

# Fit-to-width, and no pixel ceiling for vector receipts

Amends the scope of
[ADR-0006](0006-the-stored-image-is-the-contract.md). That decision's raster
reasoning stands; this one says what it is about.

## Context & decision

ADR-0006 settled two things about the viewer: 100% means fit-to-viewport, and
zoom stops at the image's own natural resolution. Both were written about a
photograph. An emailed receipt is not one — `renderTextToSvg` typesets the email
body into an SVG — and both rules fail on it.

**A vector image has no pixel ceiling.** `calculateMaxZoom` stops where one image
pixel fills one CSS pixel, which for a resolution-independent format is a
category error: there is no pixel grid to exhaust. On the reported receipt it
computed to ~128%, which is the "even after you click zoom it barely grows"
symptom exactly. Vector images get a flat **800%** ceiling instead — arbitrary,
finite only so the zoom-in button can honestly disable itself and a stray gesture
cannot ask the browser to lay out a 40,000px element.

**100% becomes fit-to-width**, `scale = min(viewportWidth / naturalWidth, 1)`,
for **all** images. Fitting the whole image inside 90vw × 80vh means the height
binds for any tall document, so a 1100 × 2000 SVG landed ~530px wide and its own
`font-size` cancelled out. This is not an SVG problem — a photo of a long CVS
receipt failed identically.

Neither breaks the "zoom never invents pixels" invariant. Fit-to-width still caps
`scale` at 1, so nothing is ever painted past native; and an SVG has no pixels to
invent. The invariant is a statement about raster images, and a
resolution-independent format falls outside it.

## Considered options

- **A `height/width > 2.0` threshold**, applying fit-to-width only to tall
  images. Rejected: an arbitrary constant would need defending forever, and a
  receipt at 1.9 would behave differently from one at 2.1 for no perceptible
  reason.
- **Fit-to-width for vector only.** Rejected: it knowingly leaves the identical
  bug in place for long photographs, which is where it was first reachable.
- **Persist the email text and render it as real HTML in the viewer.** The design
  that is actually right — a text email is text, and it would be selectable,
  searchable and reflowable. Rejected here as needing a schema change plus a new
  display branch on every surface that shows a receipt, for the same user-visible
  outcome. In the [backlog](../product-backlog.md).
- **Editing ADR-0006 in place.** Rejected: it would rewrite an accepted decision
  whose raster reasoning was correct for the case it was written about. The
  failure mode an ADR prevents here is concrete — someone reads "zoom stops at
  the image's own natural resolution", sees the viewer letting an SVG past 100%,
  and files it as a regression.

## Consequences

- **A tall photograph now opens with its bottom below the fold.** A 2400 × 3200
  receipt opens ~1411px wide where it previously opened fully visible at ~725px.
  Accepted: at 80vh it was already "visible but not readable". The glance test —
  _is this the right receipt?_ — belongs to the thumbnail; the viewer exists for
  reading.
- **Tall receipts will not scroll on a phone.** `touch-action: none` on the
  backdrop plus a drag handler that only engages above 100% worked only because
  fit-to-box guaranteed the image always fitted. Deferred by decision, in the
  backlog; desktop is unaffected. The fix is `touch-action: pan-x pan-y` and
  deleting the single-finger drag emulation, which also _removes_ code and buys
  momentum scrolling.
- **The viewer needs to be told which kind of image it has.** It receives only a
  signed URL, so `isVector` is passed as a prop from `ReceiptEditModal`,
  mirroring `isPdf`.
- **`VIEWPORT_FRACTION` loses its height.** Nothing computes against the viewport
  height any more, so the vertical bound is now a `max-h-[80vh]` class like the
  PDF branch already used, and the constant is a scalar
  `VIEWPORT_WIDTH_FRACTION`.
- **Wheel zoom is now modifier-gated.** A plain wheel scrolls the container
  natively; `ctrlKey`/`metaKey` + wheel zooms, continuously rather than in 50%
  steps. macOS synthesizes `ctrlKey` for trackpad pinch, so that gesture starts
  working as a side effect. A plain mouse wheel no longer zooms.

content.content: 1 # Receipt Image Resize & Zoom Design 2 3 **Date:** 2026-08-03 4 **Status:** ✅ Built (pending release) — gate moved after resize with a 25MB decode 5 guard, 2400px @ 85%, HEIC/PNG transcoded to JPEG, zoom ceiling derived per image, 6 `/admin/resize-images` deleted. The two [open questions](#open-questions) below 7 are still open. 8 9 Resize-on-upload and zoom both already ship (`901b670`). This is a correction to 10 both, driven by a real failure: a phone photo was refused with "Image too large. 11 Max 5MB." by the line immediately before the one that would have shrunk it to 12 ~400KB. 13 14 The governing decision — the size limit describes the **Receipt Image** we store, 15 not the **Source File** we are handed — is recorded in 16 [ADR-0006](../adr/0006-the-stored-image-is-the-contract.md), with the vocabulary 17 and invariants in [the domain model](../domain-model.md). This document is the 18 implementation shape. 19 20 ## The defect 21 22 ``` 23 uploadAndCreate() ReceiptService.ts:186 24 ├─ validateFile(file) :187 ← rejects Source File > 5MB 25 └─ withRetry( :190 26 prepareFileForUpload() :191 ← resize to 2000px / 85% 27 uploadToStorage() :192 28 ``` 29 30 `validateFile` (`:164`) reads `file.size` on the picked file. `MAX_IMAGE_MB = 5` 31 (`:13`) is small next to a modern phone photo — 3–5MB typically, 8–12MB at 48MP — 32 so the gate fires on files the pipeline exists to shrink. 33 34 Nothing downstream rescues it. `FileValidator` 35 (`src/lib/server/fileValidation.ts:13`, 10MB, magic-number based) is server-side 36 and not on this path. The email-ingestion path (`supabase/functions/resend/handler.ts:137`) 37 has no size check at all, so the same receipt forwarded by email is accepted at 38 full size while the upload button refuses it. 39 40 ## Changes 41 42 ### 1. Validation splits in two 43 44 `validateFile` currently answers one question with three checks. It becomes two 45 gates around the resize: 46 47 **Before decode** — file type against the allow-list, plus a **25MB** ceiling on 48 any type. This ceiling is a memory guard, not a policy about receipts: it stops a 49 200MP panorama or a RAW export from hanging the tab before Canvas is even 50 reached. Comfortably above a 48MP iPhone photo and a multi-page scanned PDF. 51 52 **After resize** — the existing `MAX_IMAGE_MB` (5) / `MAX_PDF_MB` (10) applied to 53 the file actually being uploaded. 54 55 Note the shift in what a rejection _means_. `prepareFileForUpload` swallows any 56 resize error and returns the original (`:215`), so a 12MB photo whose resize 57 fails — Canvas OOM, a corrupt EXIF block, HEIC on a non-Apple browser — now falls 58 back to a 12MB original that the second gate refuses. The file is refused either 59 way, but the reason is "we could not shrink this", and the message must say that 60 rather than repeating "too large", which would send the person off to do 61 something that will not help. 62 63 ### 2. Resize accepts HEIC and PNG, and always emits JPEG 64 65 `resizeImage` returns early for anything that is not JPEG or PNG 66 (`imageResize.ts:72`), while the upload control offers `image/heic` 67 (`src/routes/receipts/+page.svelte:492`). Two independent problems follow from 68 the format handling: 69 70 - **HEIC is skipped entirely** — the backlog has flagged this as unverified 71 on-device since the mobile-capture PRD. Safari (macOS/iOS) can decode HEIC into 72 Canvas and Chrome/Firefox cannot, which is fortunate: HEIC only originates on 73 Apple platforms. Feed it through the same path and fall back to the untouched 74 original elsewhere. 75 - **PNG is never compressed.** `canvas.toBlob(cb, file.type, quality)` (`:104`) 76 ignores the quality argument for lossless formats, so 85% has never applied to 77 a PNG. There is also no keep-the-smaller-file guard, so a sub-threshold PNG is 78 re-encoded at identical dimensions and returned even when the result is bigger 79 than what the person picked. Screenshots of e-receipts are usually PNG. 80 81 Both dissolve if the output is always JPEG. `toBlob` is called with 82 `'image/jpeg'` regardless of input, and the storage path extension follows. 83 84 `original_filename` is unaffected and must stay that way — it deliberately 85 captures the pre-resize name (`#{#ofn2a}`, `ReceiptService.ts:283`) so a receipt 86 is listed under the name its owner recognizes, even though the stored object is 87 now `.jpg`. 88 89 **Consequential fix:** `extractReceiptDataFailSoft(path, file.type)` (`:193`) 90 passes the _original_ file's MIME type while the object at `path` is the resized 91 one. Harmless today; a live bug the moment HEIC transcodes, because OCR would be 92 told `image/heic` about a JPEG. It must take the uploaded file's type. 93 94 ### 3. Pixel budget: 2400px longest axis at 85% 95 96 Up from 2000px, for headroom on receipts photographed at a distance, where the 97 receipt occupies a fraction of the frame. Expected stored size ~500–800KB. 98 99 The comment at `imageResize.ts:58` ("Images smaller than 2000px still have 100 compression applied") is false for PNG today and should be corrected rather than 101 carried forward. 102 103 ### 4. Zoom stops at native resolution 104 105 `ReceiptImageViewer.svelte` fits the image to the viewport at 100% 106 (`handleImageLoad`, `:72`) and caps at a flat `MAX_ZOOM = 400` (`:56`). Those two 107 constants were chosen independently and disagree: a 2400×1000 receipt on a 108 1440px-tall laptop fits at ~1150px, so 100% is ~48% of native and 400% asks the 109 browser to paint ~4800px from a 2400px file. Everything past roughly 210% is 110 interpolation. On a phone the same 400% lands near 1:1, so the current constant 111 is approximately right there and badly wrong on a desktop. 112 113 `MAX_ZOOM` becomes derived: `100 × naturalWidth / baseWidth`, the zoom at which 114 one image pixel occupies one CSS pixel. 115 116 `ZOOM_STEP` is 50 and `zoomIn`/`zoomOut` snap to multiples of it (`:127`, 117 `:134`), so the derived ceiling will rarely be a multiple of 50 — the top step 118 must clamp to the ceiling rather than skip past or become unreachable. 119 120 Where the fit scale is already clamped at 1 (`:78`) — any image at or below 121 viewport size — the ceiling equals `MIN_ZOOM` and both buttons sit permanently 122 disabled. That is the accepted outcome, not an edge case to patch: there are no 123 further real pixels, and the disabled control says so. It affects small PNGs and 124 low-resolution receipts uploaded before resizing existed. 125 126 ### 5. Delete `/admin/resize-images` 127 128 A one-off migration page (~260 lines) whose job is finished. It would now do 129 active harm — it re-resizes at its own hardcoded constants, permanently 130 destroying the extra detail in pre-`901b670` full-resolution originals that the 131 native-resolution zoom ceiling is designed to exploit. It is also the 132 unauthenticated delete-and-reupload route recorded as **M2** in the 133 [backlog](../product-backlog.md); deleting it closes the finding outright. 134 135 Removing it also removes the second caller of `resizeImage`, so the new 136 constants have exactly one call site. 137 138 ### No backfill 139 140 Storage will hold three generations of Receipt Image — full-resolution from 141 before `901b670`, 2000px since, 2400px after this change. A ceiling derived from 142 each image's own dimensions handles all three correctly with no migration; the 143 older full-resolution receipts simply permit more zoom. 144 145 ## What is deliberately not changing 146 147 - **The email path.** `handler.ts:137` uploads attachment bytes straight to 148 storage, unresized and ungated. It is a Deno edge function with no Canvas, so 149 matching this behaviour means a WASM image library plus a second copy of the 150 resize rules in `supabase/functions/_shared/`, kept in lock-step by hand — the 151 same maintenance burden CLAUDE.md already flags for the date-correction code, 152 and CPU time inside a webhook that must answer quickly. Logged as a backlog 153 item instead. 154 - **PDFs.** Stored as received, gated at 10MB, no zoom in the viewer 155 (`isPdf`, delegated to the browser's PDF renderer). 156 157 ## One deviation from the design as agreed 158 159 The design said resize would stay inside `withRetry`, re-decoding on each attempt 160 — wasteful but harmless. Moving validation after the resize changed that 161 calculus: a size rejection thrown inside `withRetry` would be retried three times 162 with backoff, so the person waits ~2.8 seconds per file for a verdict that could 163 not change. Both the resize and the artifact check now sit **outside** the retry, 164 which leaves the network steps (upload → OCR → insert) as the only retried work 165 and incidentally removes the repeated decode. Nothing that was retried before has 166 stopped being retried. 167 168 ## Memory 169 170 `resizeImage` decodes the file twice: it builds an `` from an object URL 171 purely to get an `onload` (`:77`, `:152`), then ignores that element and decodes 172 the same bytes again via `createImageBitmap(file)` (`:89`). Peak memory is 173 doubled on exactly the large files the 25MB ceiling now admits, and on an older 174 phone that is the difference between working and a crashed tab. The `` is 175 removable — `createImageBitmap` is itself the decode and needs no prior load 176 event. This is a correctness prerequisite for raising the ceiling, not a 177 tidy-up. 178 179 In its favour: `processUploadBatch` (`src/lib/utils/batchUpload.ts:44`) is a 180 sequential `for…of await`, so a multi-file selection never holds more than one 181 decode at a time. 182 183 ## Testing 184 185 - `imageResize.spec.ts` (node) — dimension maths at the new 2400px threshold, the 186 accepted-type list, the JPEG renaming rule, and that HEIC reaches 187 `createImageBitmap` with `imageOrientation: 'from-image'` rather than being 188 skipped. 189 - `imageResize.svelte.spec.ts` (**browser**) — the function's body. The 190 `.svelte.spec.ts` suffix is the only route into the Chromium project; in node 191 `createImageBitmap` and `document` are both undefined, so without this file 192 `resizeImage` never actually executes anywhere and transcoding is unverified. 193 Asserts on the produced file: JPEG type and `.jpg` name, longest axis capped at 194 2400px with the ratio preserved, a photo shrinking by more than half, and a 195 transparent PNG landing on **white** rather than black. 196 - `ReceiptService.uploadValidation.spec.ts` — a Source File over 5MB but under 197 25MB now succeeds (the reported failure, as a regression test); over 25MB is 198 refused before `resizeImage` is called at all; a transcoded file over 5MB is 199 still refused; a resize failure on a large file is refused with the 200 shrink-failure message and on a small one falls back to the original, stored 201 under its own extension and content type; the transcode lands under a `.jpg` 202 key; the MIME sent to OCR matches what storage received. 203 - `ReceiptImageViewer.svelte.spec.ts` — ceiling derived from natural size (the 204 image is never painted wider than `naturalWidth`); controls disabled when 205 natural ≤ viewport; the clip box matches `VIEWPORT_FRACTION`. 206 - Manual, on-device: an iPhone upload end-to-end, plus the gesture check already 207 standing in the backlog (wheel/drag/pinch after the a11y action refactor). 208 209 Note the browser project is advisory only — Vercel's `buildCommand` runs 210 `vitest run --project server` ([ADR-0005](../adr/0005-quality-gate-in-the-vercel-build-not-github-actions.md)), 211 so the transcode and zoom-ceiling tests gate nothing. That is the standing 212 trade-off, not something specific to this change. 213 214 ## Known limits, deliberately left 215 216 - **The fit is computed once, at image load.** `baseWidth`/`baseHeight` come from 217 the window size at the moment the receipt decodes, and nothing recomputes them 218 on resize, so after resizing the window the receipt no longer fills the 219 intended fraction. The same 224 exposure existed under the old 5MB cap, five times smaller; a pixel-count guard 225 would need the dimensions, which are only known after the decode starts. 226 227 ## Open questions 228 229 1. **Does 2400px buy OCR anything?** Mistral's vision model downscales large 230 inputs internally; if its effective ceiling is ~1024–1500px on an axis, the 231 extra pixels serve human zoom only. file.content: # Receipt Image Resize & Zoom Design **Date:** 2026-08-03 **Status:** ✅ Built (pending release) — gate moved after resize with a 25MB decode guard, 2400px @ 85%, HEIC/PNG transcoded to JPEG, zoom ceiling derived per image, `/admin/resize-images` deleted. The two [open questions](#open-questions) below are still open. Resize-on-upload and zoom both already ship (`901b670`). This is a correction to both, driven by a real failure: a phone photo was refused with "Image too large. Max 5MB." by the line immediately before the one that would have shrunk it to ~400KB. The governing decision — the size limit describes the **Receipt Image** we store, not the **Source File** we are handed — is recorded in [ADR-0006](../adr/0006-the-stored-image-is-the-contract.md), with the vocabulary and invariants in [the domain model](../domain-model.md). This document is the implementation shape. ## The defect ``` uploadAndCreate() ReceiptService.ts:186 ├─ validateFile(file) :187 ← rejects Source File > 5MB └─ withRetry( :190 prepareFileForUpload() :191 ← resize to 2000px / 85% uploadToStorage() :192 ``` `validateFile` (`:164`) reads `file.size` on the picked file. `MAX_IMAGE_MB = 5` (`:13`) is small next to a modern phone photo — 3–5MB typically, 8–12MB at 48MP — so the gate fires on files the pipeline exists to shrink. Nothing downstream rescues it. `FileValidator` (`src/lib/server/fileValidation.ts:13`, 10MB, magic-number based) is server-side and not on this path. The email-ingestion path (`supabase/functions/resend/handler.ts:137`) has no size check at all, so the same receipt forwarded by email is accepted at full size while the upload button refuses it. ## Changes ### 1. Validation splits in two `validateFile` currently answers one question with three checks. It becomes two gates around the resize: **Before decode** — file type against the allow-list, plus a **25MB** ceiling on any type. This ceiling is a memory guard, not a policy about receipts: it stops a 200MP panorama or a RAW export from hanging the tab before Canvas is even reached. Comfortably above a 48MP iPhone photo and a multi-page scanned PDF. **After resize** — the existing `MAX_IMAGE_MB` (5) / `MAX_PDF_MB` (10) applied to the file actually being uploaded. Note the shift in what a rejection _means_. `prepareFileForUpload` swallows any resize error and returns the original (`:215`), so a 12MB photo whose resize fails — Canvas OOM, a corrupt EXIF block, HEIC on a non-Apple browser — now falls back to a 12MB original that the second gate refuses. The file is refused either way, but the reason is "we could not shrink this", and the message must say that rather than repeating "too large", which would send the person off to do something that will not help. ### 2. Resize accepts HEIC and PNG, and always emits JPEG `resizeImage` returns early for anything that is not JPEG or PNG (`imageResize.ts:72`), while the upload control offers `image/heic` (`src/routes/receipts/+page.svelte:492`). Two independent problems follow from the format handling: - **HEIC is skipped entirely** — the backlog has flagged this as unverified on-device since the mobile-capture PRD. Safari (macOS/iOS) can decode HEIC into Canvas and Chrome/Firefox cannot, which is fortunate: HEIC only originates on Apple platforms. Feed it through the same path and fall back to the untouched original elsewhere. - **PNG is never compressed.** `canvas.toBlob(cb, file.type, quality)` (`:104`) ignores the quality argument for lossless formats, so 85% has never applied to a PNG. There is also no keep-the-smaller-file guard, so a sub-threshold PNG is re-encoded at identical dimensions and returned even when the result is bigger than what the person picked. Screenshots of e-receipts are usually PNG. Both dissolve if the output is always JPEG. `toBlob` is called with `'image/jpeg'` regardless of input, and the storage path extension follows. `original_filename` is unaffected and must stay that way — it deliberately captures the pre-resize name (`#{#ofn2a}`, `ReceiptService.ts:283`) so a receipt is listed under the name its owner recognizes, even though the stored object is now `.jpg`. **Consequential fix:** `extractReceiptDataFailSoft(path, file.type)` (`:193`) passes the _original_ file's MIME type while the object at `path` is the resized one. Harmless today; a live bug the moment HEIC transcodes, because OCR would be told `image/heic` about a JPEG. It must take the uploaded file's type. ### 3. Pixel budget: 2400px longest axis at 85% Up from 2000px, for headroom on receipts photographed at a distance, where the receipt occupies a fraction of the frame. Expected stored size ~500–800KB. The comment at `imageResize.ts:58` ("Images smaller than 2000px still have compression applied") is false for PNG today and should be corrected rather than carried forward. ### 4. Zoom stops at native resolution `ReceiptImageViewer.svelte` fits the image to the viewport at 100% (`handleImageLoad`, `:72`) and caps at a flat `MAX_ZOOM = 400` (`:56`). Those two constants were chosen independently and disagree: a 2400×1000 receipt on a 1440px-tall laptop fits at ~1150px, so 100% is ~48% of native and 400% asks the browser to paint ~4800px from a 2400px file. Everything past roughly 210% is interpolation. On a phone the same 400% lands near 1:1, so the current constant is approximately right there and badly wrong on a desktop. `MAX_ZOOM` becomes derived: `100 × naturalWidth / baseWidth`, the zoom at which one image pixel occupies one CSS pixel. `ZOOM_STEP` is 50 and `zoomIn`/`zoomOut` snap to multiples of it (`:127`, `:134`), so the derived ceiling will rarely be a multiple of 50 — the top step must clamp to the ceiling rather than skip past or become unreachable. Where the fit scale is already clamped at 1 (`:78`) — any image at or below viewport size — the ceiling equals `MIN_ZOOM` and both buttons sit permanently disabled. That is the accepted outcome, not an edge case to patch: there are no further real pixels, and the disabled control says so. It affects small PNGs and low-resolution receipts uploaded before resizing existed. ### 5. Delete `/admin/resize-images` A one-off migration page (~260 lines) whose job is finished. It would now do active harm — it re-resizes at its own hardcoded constants, permanently destroying the extra detail in pre-`901b670` full-resolution originals that the native-resolution zoom ceiling is designed to exploit. It is also the unauthenticated delete-and-reupload route recorded as **M2** in the [backlog](../product-backlog.md); deleting it closes the finding outright. Removing it also removes the second caller of `resizeImage`, so the new constants have exactly one call site. ### No backfill Storage will hold three generations of Receipt Image — full-resolution from before `901b670`, 2000px since, 2400px after this change. A ceiling derived from each image's own dimensions handles all three correctly with no migration; the older full-resolution receipts simply permit more zoom. ## What is deliberately not changing - **The email path.** `handler.ts:137` uploads attachment bytes straight to storage, unresized and ungated. It is a Deno edge function with no Canvas, so matching this behaviour means a WASM image library plus a second copy of the resize rules in `supabase/functions/_shared/`, kept in lock-step by hand — the same maintenance burden CLAUDE.md already flags for the date-correction code, and CPU time inside a webhook that must answer quickly. Logged as a backlog item instead. - **PDFs.** Stored as received, gated at 10MB, no zoom in the viewer (`isPdf`, delegated to the browser's PDF renderer). ## One deviation from the design as agreed The design said resize would stay inside `withRetry`, re-decoding on each attempt — wasteful but harmless. Moving validation after the resize changed that calculus: a size rejection thrown inside `withRetry` would be retried three times with backoff, so the person waits ~2.8 seconds per file for a verdict that could not change. Both the resize and the artifact check now sit **outside** the retry, which leaves the network steps (upload → OCR → insert) as the only retried work and incidentally removes the repeated decode. Nothing that was retried before has stopped being retried. ## Memory `resizeImage` decodes the file twice: it builds an `` from an object URL purely to get an `onload` (`:77`, `:152`), then ignores that element and decodes the same bytes again via `createImageBitmap(file)` (`:89`). Peak memory is doubled on exactly the large files the 25MB ceiling now admits, and on an older phone that is the difference between working and a crashed tab. The `` is removable — `createImageBitmap` is itself the decode and needs no prior load event. This is a correctness prerequisite for raising the ceiling, not a tidy-up. In its favour: `processUploadBatch` (`src/lib/utils/batchUpload.ts:44`) is a sequential `for…of await`, so a multi-file selection never holds more than one decode at a time. ## Testing - `imageResize.spec.ts` (node) — dimension maths at the new 2400px threshold, the accepted-type list, the JPEG renaming rule, and that HEIC reaches `createImageBitmap` with `imageOrientation: 'from-image'` rather than being skipped. - `imageResize.svelte.spec.ts` (**browser**) — the function's body. Asserts on the produced file: JPEG type and `.jpg` name, longest axis capped at 2400px with the ratio preserved, a photo shrinking by more than half, and a transparent PNG landing on **white** rather than black. - `ReceiptService.uploadValidation.spec.ts` — a Source File over 5MB but under 25MB now succeeds (the reported failure, as a regression test); over 25MB is refused before `resizeImage` is called at all; a transcoded file over 5MB is still refused; a resize failure on a large file is refused with the shrink-failure message and on a small one falls back to the original, stored under its own extension and content type; the transcode lands under a `.jpg` key; the MIME sent to OCR matches what storage received. - `ReceiptImageViewer.svelte.spec.ts` — ceiling derived from natural size (the image is never painted wider than `naturalWidth`); controls disabled when natural ≤ viewport; the clip box matches `VIEWPORT_FRACTION`. - Manual, on-device: an iPhone upload end-to-end, plus the gesture check already standing in the backlog (wheel/drag/pinch after the a11y action refactor). The 1:1 ceiling stays exact regardless (it is derived from the same `baseWidth` used to scale), so the "never invents pixels" invariant holds — only the fit goes stale. Pre-existing behaviour, unchanged here. - **`MAX_SOURCE_MB` guards bytes, but decode cost is driven by pixels.** A well-compressed 3MB 12000×9000 scan still allocates ~430MB of RGBA. # Receipt Notes — Design

**Date:** 2026-08-03
**Status:** ✅ **Done** — all eight sequencing steps landed 2026-08-03 (pending
release). `receipts.notes` + CHECK, the `Note (optional)` textarea with counter and
save-gating, previews on both list pages, splits copying the note, and
`buildReceiptPatch` replacing the three page-level patch literals. The two live bugs
this design uncovered (§5 and the `original_filename` half of §6) were fixed first,
ahead of the feature.

**One verification step was still outstanding when this closed:** `npm run db:reset`
has **not** been run against the migration — Docker was unavailable on both attempts.
====
# Emailed Receipt Legibility Design

**Date:** 2026-08-03
**Status:** ✅ Built (pending release), with four deviations noted at the end. The
[known regression](#known-regression-shipped-deliberately) shipped as designed.
The backfill ran once and the script was deleted, as designed — what remains of it
is the `data-yfl-render-version` marker on every stored SVG.

A receipt forwarded by email arrives as an unreadable thumbnail, and clicking
through to the zoom viewer barely helps — the viewer refuses to magnify it past
~128%. Three independent causes, in three different files, none of which is the
one the symptom points at.

## Open questions

- **Should notes be searchable?** Deferred from [Receipt Notes](plans-done/2026-08-03-receipt-notes-design.md). Neither list page has free-text search today — Receipts filters on merchant/amount/needs-review/duplicates, Expenses on date/category/uncategorized — so searching notes is a **new capability**, not an extension of an existing control, and it would want an index on `receipts.notes` (which the design deliberately omits). Worth revisiting once there are enough notes to lose one in.
- **Combining receipts for one expense.** How to handle when two receipts should be combined into one expense to match — e.g. two medications picked up at the same time.
- **WealthSimple refund handling.** WealthSimple records several rows when a refund is issued. Example:

  ```csv
  "2026-05-24","2026-05-24","Refund initiated","MARSHES GOLF CORPORATI","-33.9","CAD"
  "2026-05-24","2026-05-25","Refund settled","MARSHES GOLF CORPORATI","33.9","CAD"
  "2026-05-24","2026-05-25","Refund settled","MARSHES GOLF CORPORATI","-33.9","CAD"
  ```

content.content:
## Engineering

### In progress

- **🟢 Bombadil property-based UI testing (spike) — built and running.** `bombadil/transactions.ts` explores `/transactions` against the local stack with 12 properties (the 4 free ones plus a pathname tripwire, filter/counter/selection invariants). Session comes from a DEV-and-loopback-gated auto-login (`src/lib/dev/autoLogin.ts`); `npm run bombadil` after `npm run db:fresh` + `npm run dev`. A clean 60-second run explores ~390 actions (≈5/sec) with no violations. Open follow-ups: **`PressKey` wedges the run** — every run including it hung with the browser at 100% CPU, so keyboard interaction is excluded entirely and the cause is undiagnosed; **native `<select>` popups hang it too**, so the card/bank-type filter is unexplored (Chrome renders the option list outside the page); **Delete / bulk-delete are excluded** because they use `confirm()`; and **`--reproduce` has never been exercised**. Widening to a second page (which means a second hand-written specification, not a config change) and deciding whether it earns a nightly GitHub Action (`antithesishq/bombadil-action@v2`) are the next questions. See [Bombadil spike handoff](plans-done/2026-07-26-bombadil-property-testing-spike.md).

### Security

- **🟠 HIGH — unverified, non-unique profile emails allow email-ingestion hijack.** _(Found 2026-07-17 audit; the top open security item.)_ The add-email flow (`src/routes/profile/+page.svelte`) lets a user attach ANY address to their profile (`profiles.email_1..5`) with only format + within-own-profile dedup — **no ownership verification and no cross-user unique constraint**. The Resend webhook attributes inbound receipts via `find_user_by_email(sender)`, which falls through to those profile columns (`resend/handler.ts`). So an attacker can claim a victim's forwarding/secondary address and have the victim's forwarded receipts ingested into the attacker's account (data leak), or make attribution nondeterministic (`limit 1`) when two profiles claim the same address, or pre-claim an address to poison a future user. Not closed by the webhook-signature fix — the abuse is by a legitimately authed user. Fix: confirm ownership via emailed token before an alias participates in lookup; add a global `UNIQUE(lower(email))` (ideally a normalized `profile_emails` table); prefer exact `auth.users` identity over unverified aliases.
- **Sweep the remaining `SECURITY DEFINER` functions for missing `anon` revokes.** The seed-function lockdown found that `REVOKE … FROM PUBLIC` left a _direct_ `anon` grant in place, needing an explicit `REVOKE … FROM anon`. Only `create_default_hierarchy` / `create_default_categories` were fixed that way. Audit every other `SECURITY DEFINER` function for the same hole and revoke explicitly where `authenticated` is the only legitimate caller.
- **🟢 LOW / deferred audit items (re-verified 2026-07-17).** Unchanged since the 2026-07-05 audit — see the [Security Remediation PRD "Deferred" section](prd-done/prd-security-remediation.md): **H3** `/api/ocr` + `/api/ocr/extract` are unauthenticated and SSRF-able via a caller-supplied `fileUrl` (no auth, no host allow-list — `src/routes/api/ocr/**`); **M1** the Resend webhook still logs full request headers (`resend/handler.ts:334`, including svix signature material) and an API-key prefix/suffix (`:389`); **M3** the `families` INSERT policy is `WITH CHECK (auth.uid() IS NOT NULL)` only (no `created_by` binding, no limit); **F6** `email_send_failures` SELECT is whole-family-scoped, so co-members can read each other's notification recipient + subject — confirm that's intended.

### Dependencies

- **High vuln: `xlsx` (SheetJS) has no npm fix — decision needed.** `npm audit` reports 1 high against `xlsx@^0.18.5` — Prototype Pollution ([GHSA-4r6h-8v6p-xvw6](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-4r6h-8v6p-xvw6), fixed in 0.19.3) and ReDoS ([GHSA-5pgg-2g8v-p4x9](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-5pgg-2g8v-p4x9), fixed in 0.20.2). Both fixes exist **only on the SheetJS CDN (`cdn.sheetjs.com`), not npm** — the npm package is unmaintained, so `npm audit` will never clear and there is no version to bump to. Used only by the Excel importer, contained in `src/lib/services/ExcelToCSVConverter.ts` behind a stable interface; the app supports **both** legacy `.xls` (BIFF8) and `.xlsx`. Options: (a) pin the CDN tarball via `overrides` — clears the CVEs and keeps `.xls`, but adds a non-registry dep our `min-release-age` hardening can't gate; (b) migrate to `exceljs` — maintained, but **cannot read legacy `.xls`**, so it drops that support unless paired with a BIFF parser. **The decision to make: is legacy `.xls` still required?** Deferred — the importer is not internet-exposed (users upload their own bank exports), which lowers practical risk.
- **Low vulns: `cookie` (via `@sveltejs/kit`) and `esbuild` dev server.** (1) `cookie <0.7.0` accepts out-of-bounds characters in name/path/domain ([GHSA-pxg6-pf52-xh8x](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-pxg6-pf52-xh8x)), pulled in transitively through `@sveltejs/kit` → `@sveltejs/adapter-auto` / `runed` / `layerchart`; `npm audit fix --force` would downgrade `@sveltejs/kit` to `1.0.0-next.0` (breaking), so wait for the framework chain to bump `cookie`. (2) `esbuild 0.27.3–0.28.0` allows arbitrary file read when the dev server runs on Windows ([GHSA-g7r4-m6w7-qqqr](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-g7r4-m6w7-qqqr)) — dev-only, non-Windows here; clearable with a plain `npm audit fix`. Low priority; both are dev/transitive, not shipped to users.
- **🔴 New since the last audit: 6 further `npm audit` findings, 2 of them critical.** _(Surfaced 2026-07-26 while adding the Bombadil dev dependency; none introduced by it — `@antithesishq/bombadil` has zero dependencies. The total is now 9: 2 low, 1 moderate, 4 high, 2 critical.)_ Every one claims a fix via a plain `npm audit fix`, so this is mostly a bump-and-verify job — but it needs the fixes actually applied and the suites re-run, not just logged.
  - **CRITICAL — `@vitest/browser <=3.2.6`:** Browser Mode provider commands bypass the file-access permission gate ([GHSA-p63j-vcc4-9vmv](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-p63j-vcc4-9vmv)). Two advisories, counted against both `@vitest/browser` and `vitest`. We run browser-mode tests, so this is the one to fix first.
  - **MODERATE — `@sveltejs/kit <=2.70.1`:** prototype pollution in the remote-function form file-input deletion path ([GHSA-866w-xmhq-wj7x](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-866w-xmhq-wj7x)), plus a Node crash on large remote-form payloads ([GHSA-wqjv-9729-c5q2](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-wqjv-9729-c5q2)). We don't use remote functions today, but this is shipped framework code.

### Security

- **🟠 HIGH — unverified, non-unique profile emails allow email-ingestion hijack.** _(Found 2026-07-17 audit; the top open security item.)_ The add-email flow (`src/routes/profile/+page.svelte`) lets a user attach ANY address to their profile (`profiles.email_1..5`) with only format + within-own-profile dedup — **no ownership verification and no cross-user unique constraint**. Two esbuild copies exist in the lockfile — `0.27.7` at the root (used by Vite/Vitest, approved) and `0.28.1` nested under `tsx` (not approved). The current CI job is unaffected because `npm run verify` never invokes `tsx`, but the `seed:demo` scripts do. Either approve `esbuild@0.28.1` or confirm the nested copy works without its postinstall.
- **Watch for storage-policy drift.** `supabase db dump` does not cover the `storage` schema, so the `receipts` bucket + its 4 policies are hand-maintained at the end of `20260726120000_baseline.sql`. A future storage change written only as a migration will be lost the next time the baseline is regenerated; one made only in the dashboard will never reach a new environment. Consider a check that diffs live storage policies against the baseline.
- **Emailed receipts are never resized — the two capture paths store different things.** The Resend handler uploads attachment bytes straight to storage (`supabase/functions/resend/handler.ts:137`) with no size check and no resize, so a receipt forwarded by email is stored at whatever size the sender's mail client produced, while the same receipt uploaded in the browser becomes a 2400px JPEG. Deliberate for now — it is a Deno edge function with no Canvas, so matching it means a WASM image library plus a second copy of the resize rules in `supabase/functions/_shared/` kept in lock-step by hand (the burden CLAUDE.md already flags for the date-correction code), and CPU time inside a webhook that must answer quickly. Revisit if storage cost or emailed-receipt volume grows.

Unit tests cover logic, not real gestures — manually confirm wheel-zoom, drag-to-pan, pinch-zoom, and keyboard/screen-reader access still work. **Extended 2026-08-03:** the wheel path is now modifier-gated and continuous, so also confirm that a plain mouse wheel and a two-finger trackpad scroll _scroll_, that trackpad pinch zooms smoothly rather than in 50% lurches, and that Ctrl/Cmd + wheel zooms toward the cursor.

A pathological forwarded thread could produce a document tall enough that browsers refuse to rasterize it. No cap was added deliberately — the whole point of the change was to stop losing content — so the fix, if it is ever needed, is pagination or a "… N further lines" marker, not silent truncation.
- **`ReceiptService` ships debug logging to production.** Three `console.log`s on the receipts-page load path (`src/lib/services/ReceiptService.ts:84`, `:91`, `:101`) print the user id, the **full `family_members` rows for that user**, and the fetched receipt payload to the browser console on every visit. The middle one is a query run purely to log its result — it is labelled "for debugging" and nothing consumes it. A fourth logs every created receipt in `insertReceiptOrCleanupUpload` (`:347`); it is the only remaining reader of `family_id` on `InsertedReceiptRow`, so deleting it may let that type collapse back to `ReceiptRow`. Delete the logs and the debug query.
- **Receipts page fetches every family expense just to colour one column.** `loadCategories` (`src/routes/receipts/+page.svelte:254`) calls `ExpenseService.getExpenses` — a full paged pass over `receipts` with an embed — solely to build `categoryMap`. It should read `expense_categories` for the receipts already in hand instead.

# The stored image is the contract

> **Scope amended by
> [ADR-0007](0007-fit-to-width-and-a-vector-zoom-ceiling.md).** Everything below
> is about _raster_ receipts. 100% is now fit-to-_width_, and an emailed receipt
> — an SVG — has no pixel ceiling to stop at.

## Context & decision

`ReceiptService.uploadAndCreate()` validated the file the person picked and
_then_ shrank it. The 5MB limit therefore measured the **Source File** while the
resize that would have made it ~400KB ran on the next line.

The fix is to decide what the limit is _about_. **The limit describes the
artifact we keep, not the artifact we are handed.** Size validation moves after
the resize, so it gates the **Receipt Image**; the Source File is bounded only by
a 25MB pre-decode ceiling that exists to protect the browser's memory, not to
judge the receipt. Everything follows from that principle:

- **2400px longest axis at 85% JPEG.** The stored image is what a person zooms
  into, so the pixel budget is chosen for human reading, not for OCR.
- **HEIC and PNG transcode to JPEG.** One stored format. PNG additionally never
  honoured the 85% quality argument (`toBlob` ignores it for lossless formats),
  so a PNG "resize" could return a file _larger_ than it arrived.
- **Zoom stops at the image's own natural resolution**, replacing a flat
  `MAX_ZOOM = 400`. 100% is fit-to-viewport, so a fixed percentage meant
  different things per device: on a phone 400% was roughly 1:1, on a desktop it
  demanded ~2.3× more detail than a 2000px file contains. The mush people saw at
  high zoom was the viewer promising pixels the resize had already discarded.
- **No backfill.** A per-image ceiling reads each generation correctly on its
  own. Re-resizing the pre-`901b670` full-resolution originals would destroy
  detail we already paid to store — so `/admin/resize-images` is deleted rather
  than updated, which also closes the **M2** finding (an unauthenticated
  delete-and-reupload page) instead of deferring it a fourth time.

## Considered options

- **Raise `MAX_IMAGE_MB` from 5 to ~15.** A one-line unblock, rejected because
  the gate would still measure the wrong artifact: a 16MB photo that resizes to
  400KB is still refused for no reason the family can perceive.
- **Keep the gate, improve the error message.** Cheapest, and the honest reading
  of it is "we have automated shrinking, and we are going to ask you to do it
  anyway."
- **Keep PNG lossless, add a keep-the-smaller-file guard.** Genuinely defensible
  — JPEG ringing around small glyphs is real, and screenshot receipts have sharp
  edges. Rejected for a single stored format; at 2400px and 85% the artefacts are
  well below the threshold that matters for reading a total.
- **Two artifacts per receipt** — a small display/OCR copy plus a large read
  copy. Best quality-per-byte, rejected as doubling the storage objects and
  adding a second signed-URL path to every surface that shows a receipt.
- **Cap zoom at ~1.5× native** rather than a hard 1:1, keeping some headroom
  because magnification past 1:1 still helps low-vision readers even though it
  adds no information. Rejected in favour of the stricter rule: every pixel on
  screen is a real pixel.

## Consequences

- **Transcoding is irreversible and lossy.** Detail discarded at upload never
  comes back — there is no original to re-derive from, by design. Revisiting the
  2400px/85% numbers only affects receipts uploaded after the change.
- **A PNG screenshot can come out _larger_ than it arrived.** JPEG spends bits on
  the hard edges of rendered text that PNG encodes almost for free, so for a
  sharp-edged e-receipt screenshot already within the pixel budget the transcode
  can grow the file. Measured, not theoretical. This is the cost of the single
  stored format and is accepted; the keep-the-smaller-file guard above is the
  alternative if it ever matters. Photographs — the overwhelming majority —
  shrink by well over half.
- **JPEG has no alpha, so the canvas must be painted white first.** A
  transparent-background PNG composites onto _black_ by default (the HTML spec
  requires it), which would store dark text on a black field as the only copy of
  the receipt.
- **Zoom disappears for small images.** Anything already at or below viewport
  size has `MIN_ZOOM == MAX_ZOOM` and both controls sit disabled. Accepted
  deliberately over faking magnification.
- **A resize failure now becomes a rejection.** `prepareFileForUpload` falls back
  to the original on any error; a 12MB original then fails the post-resize gate.
  The file is refused either way, but the real reason is "we could not shrink
  it", and the message must say so rather than blaming the file's size.
- **The email path diverges.** The Resend handler uploads attachment bytes
  straight to storage with no size check and no resize (Deno — no Canvas), so an
  emailed receipt is stored full-size while the same receipt uploaded in the
  browser becomes 2400px JPEG. Resizing there needs a WASM image library and a
  second copy of these rules in `supabase/functions/_shared/`, kept in lock-step
  by hand. Logged in the [backlog](../product-backlog.md) rather than built.
- **Storage now holds three generations** of Receipt Image and always will. This
  is fine for zoom (see the "Zoom never invents pixels" invariant) but means
  storage-size statistics are not comparable across upload dates.

The pixel budget was chosen for a human zooming in, not for the model ([ADR-0006](adr/0006-the-stored-image-is-the-contract.md)) — but nobody has checked what Mistral's vision model does with a large input. If it downscales internally to ~1024–1500px on an axis, the extra pixels serve human reading only. It does not change the decision; it changes the rationale, and it would let a future storage squeeze cut resolution with a known effect on extraction accuracy rather than a guessed one. Answerable from Mistral's docs.
