# PRD — Mobile Capture (single-purpose receipt capture on a phone)

- **Status:** Draft
- **Created:** 2026-07-26
- **Surface:** a new chrome-free `/capture` route; a route-group split of
  `src/routes/+layout.svelte`; a web app manifest + icons in `static/`; a queued
  wrapper around the existing `ReceiptService.uploadAndCreate()`.
- **Related:**
  - Backlog **"iPhone camera"** feature — this PRD is its concrete design, and
    deliberately answers it with a web app rather than a native iOS app.
  - [Refactoring backlog](refactoring-backlog.md) — the layout split (D2) is a
    prerequisite, not a nice-to-have.
  - Security **H3** (`/api/ocr/extract` unauthenticated + SSRF) — not caused by
    this work, but this feature adds a second high-traffic consumer of that
    endpoint. See [Security Remediation PRD](prd-done/prd-security-remediation.md).
  - [domain-model.md](domain-model.md) — Receipt, Expense terminology.

## Terminology

See [domain-model.md](domain-model.md). A **Receipt** is a row in `receipts` plus
its stored image; an **Expense** is the computed join of a receipt with its
category. This PRD introduces no new domain concepts — only a second **client
surface** onto the existing receipt-creation pipeline.

Two new UI terms, both presentational:

- **Capture screen** — the `/capture` route: one job, no navigation.
- **Upload queue** — the client-side, in-memory (later persisted) list of files
  in flight, each with its own state. Not a database concept; nothing is queued
  server-side.

content.content:
180	**The queue is presentation state, not business logic.** The state machine and
181	the concurrency policy are pure and unit-testable; the Svelte component renders
182	them. Do not put upload orchestration inside the component.
183	
184	### D5 — HEIC must not bypass the resizer
185	
186	`resizeImage()` returns the file untouched for anything that is not JPEG or PNG
187	(`src/lib/utils/imageResize.ts:71`), and `prepareFileForUpload()` skips the
188	resize call for the same set (`ReceiptService.ts:203`). Meanwhile the receipts
189	input opts **into** HEIC via its `accept` list.
190	
191	The suspected consequence: iOS Safari transcodes a picked photo to JPEG when the
192	`accept` list excludes HEIC, and hands over the original HEIC when it is
193	included. If so, today's configuration selects the one path where a full-size
194	iPhone photo goes to storage and to Mistral **unresized** — roughly a 3MB upload
195	where a 400KB one would do, on the connection least able to afford it. It also
196	sits near the 5MB image ceiling in `validateFile()`
197	(`ReceiptService.ts:170`), so a large capture can be rejected outright.
198	
199	**This is a hypothesis and must be verified on a real device before it is acted
200	on** (see **R1**). If confirmed, the capture screen omits `image/heic` from its
201	`accept` list so iOS converts to JPEG and the file flows through the existing
202	resizer. The desktop receipts page keeps HEIC in its list — a Mac user may
203	legitimately upload a `.heic` file, and there the size and bandwidth cost is not
204	a concern.
205	
206	Note the asymmetry this creates: two `accept` lists for two surfaces, for a
207	stated reason. Comment it at both sites.
208	
209	### D6 — Installability
210	
211	A manifest (`static/manifest.webmanifest`) with `name`, `short_name`,
212	`start_url: /capture`, `display: standalone`, theme/background colours, and the
213	icon set; plus `apple-touch-icon` and viewport/safe-area meta in `app.html`.
214	
215	**No service worker is required for v1.** iOS supports Add to Home Screen and
216	honours `display: standalone` from the manifest without one. A service worker is
217	introduced only if and when offline persistence (P4) is built — adding one
218	earlier buys nothing and brings a cache-invalidation problem the app does not
219	currently have.
220	
221	## Requirements
222	
223	### R1 — Verify the HEIC hypothesis (do this first)
224	
225	On a real iPhone, capture through the current receipts input and record: the
226	`File.type` and `File.size` the browser hands over, whether `prepareFileForUpload`
227	resizes, and the bytes that land in storage. Repeat with `image/heic` removed
228	from `accept`. **D5** is contingent on this result; if the behaviour differs from
229	the hypothesis, revise D5 rather than implementing it as written.

where a 400KB one would do, on the connection least able to afford it. It also
sits near the 5MB image ceiling in `validateFile()`
(`ReceiptService.ts:170`), so a large capture can be rejected outright.

**This is a hypothesis and must be verified on a real device before it is acted
on** (see **R1**). If confirmed, the capture screen omits `image/heic` from its
`accept` list so iOS converts to JPEG and the file flows through the existing
resizer. The desktop receipts page keeps HEIC in its list — a Mac user may
legitimately upload a `.heic` file, and there the size and bandwidth cost is not
a concern.

Note the asymmetry this creates: two `accept` lists for two surfaces, for a
stated reason. Comment it at both sites.

### D6 — Installability

A manifest (`static/manifest.webmanifest`) with `name`, `short_name`,
`start_url: /capture`, `display: standalone`, theme/background colours, and the
icon set; plus `apple-touch-icon` and viewport/safe-area meta in `app.html`.

**No service worker is required for v1.** iOS supports Add to Home Screen and
honours `display: standalone` from the manifest without one. A service worker is
introduced only if and when offline persistence (P4) is built — adding one
earlier buys nothing and brings a cache-invalidation problem the app does not
currently have.

## Requirements

### R1 — Verify the HEIC hypothesis (do this first)

On a real iPhone, capture through the current receipts input and record: the
`File.type` and `File.size` the browser hands over, whether `prepareFileForUpload`
resizes, and the bytes that land in storage. Repeat with `image/heic` removed
from `accept`. **D5** is contingent on this result; if the behaviour differs from
the hypothesis, revise D5 rather than implementing it as written.

content.text:
Deleted. `docs/prd-mobile-capture.md` is gone — all 359 lines of it. It was a Draft that had designed a PWA install target, a `/capture` route, a manifest, `display: standalone`, a route-group split of the layout, a service-worker deferral, an offline-capture risk assessment, and a native-vs-web platform decision. None of that was decided; it was a design for a product nobody had agreed to build.

The backlog feature is now one line saying what's actually wanted — take photos with a phone camera and upload them — and explicitly noting that the surface and screen shape are open rather than settled.

**Two references to the deleted PRD** were cleaned up in the resize plan (§2's "since the mobile-capture PRD", and the pointer I'd added to the header).

**What I kept**, because it isn't speculation about an app:

- The HEIC verification check, moved into the backlog feature line. This is a live risk in **shipped** code, not a hypothetical: if Safari doesn't decode HEIC, the resize falls back to the original and a large photo is now *refused* where it used to upload full-size. That's a regression waiting on a device, independent of any phone UI.
- Three iPhone mentions inside the done resize plan (`:57`, `:225`, `:253`). They're device facts doing real work — "48MP iPhone photo" is the sizing rationale for the 25MB ceiling, and the other two are the same on-device check. Say the word if you want those neutralized to "phone" too.

The PRD deletion is staged (`D`), recoverable with `git restore --staged --worktree docs/prd-mobile-capture.md` until you commit. Nothing is committed.
[@prd-mobile-capture.md](file:///Users/marklevison/Documents/GitHub/YFL/yfl-personal-expense-tracker/docs/prd-mobile-capture.md)
isn't dead. However mobile capture can be simple. Take picture -> upload. That's it.

## Problem

The app is usable on a phone but was not designed for one. Every route inherits
the full navigation chrome, date filters, and desktop-density tables from
`src/routes/+layout.svelte` (143 lines). The receipts page is a management
console — list, sort, edit, split, reconcile — with upload as one control among
many.

That mismatch matters because the phone use case is not "manage receipts." It is
a single five-second task, performed standing up, one-handed, often on cellular,
immediately after a purchase: **photograph this receipt and make it go away.**
Anything that asks the user to navigate, scroll past a table, or wait for an
upload before taking the next shot is friction at exactly the wrong moment — and
the observable consequence is receipts that never get captured at all.

The naive fix is "make the app responsive." That is a large job and it does not
solve this problem: a responsive `/expenses` table is still a dense multi-column
grid, and the user standing at a till does not want it at any width.

The second naive fix is a native iOS app. Assessed and rejected for v1 — see
**D1**.

- Capturing a receipt on a phone is: open icon → tap shutter → done. Five
  seconds, one hand, no navigation.
- Capturing **n** receipts in a row is **n** taps, not **n** upload-wait cycles.
- The capture surface shares one codebase, one deployment, one auth session, and
  one ingestion pipeline with the desktop app.
- The image that reaches storage is resized, regardless of what format the phone
  hands us.

  would justify it named explicitly under **Risks**.

  `/transactions`, `/reconciliation` are unchanged and remain desktop surfaces.

  reconciliation, no merchant correction beyond what **R6** decides. Review
  happens on the desktop app.
- **Offline capture.** Explicitly deferred to a later phase and constrained by a
  platform limit (**Risks**). v1 requires a live connection.
- **Changing the ingestion pipeline.** `uploadAndCreate()` keeps its current
  semantics — OCR fail-soft, orphan-blob cleanup, `withRetry`. This PRD wraps it,
  it does not rewrite it. (Moving the pipeline server-side into an Edge Function
  remains a good idea and a separate decision; it is **not** a prerequisite.)

  the only target verified.

The existing receipts input (`src/routes/receipts/+page.svelte:489`) is already a
`<input type="file" accept="image/jpeg,image/png,image/heic,application/pdf"
multiple>`. On iOS Safari that already offers **Take Photo**, **Photo Library**,
and **Choose File**. The camera is not the missing capability — the
single-purpose surface is.

/capture` and `display: standalone`, the home-screen icon opens chrome-free,
directly on the capture screen, and never reveals the expenses table or the date
filters. The desktop app stays at the normal URL.

What a native app would add, and why each is insufficient here:

| Capability                          | Web            | Native | Verdict for v1 |

| Background upload                   | ❌             | ✅     | Real, deferred |

# PRD — Mobile Capture (take a picture, upload it)

- **Status:** Draft
- **Created:** 2026-07-26
- **Rewritten:** 2026-08-03 — cut back to the actual scope. The previous draft
  designed a PWA install target, a route-group split of the layout, an upload
  queue with a state machine, a web app manifest, a service-worker deferral and a
  native-vs-web platform decision. None of that was decided, and none of it is
  needed to take a picture and upload it.
- **Related:** [domain-model.md](domain-model.md) (Receipt, Expense),
  [ADR-0006](adr/0006-the-stored-image-is-the-contract.md) (what the stored image
  is), [backlog](product-backlog.md) feature "Phone camera capture".

## Problem

The phone use case is not "manage receipts". It is a single task performed
standing up, one-handed, right after a purchase: **photograph this receipt and
make it go away.** The receipts page can do it, but it is a management console —
list, filters, sort, edit, split — with upload as one control among many, under
the full desktop navigation. Anything that asks someone to navigate or scroll
past a table at the till is friction at the wrong moment, and the consequence is
receipts that never get captured.

## Scope

Take a picture. Upload it. That is the whole feature.

Everything else about phones is **undecided, not designed**: whether it installs
to the home screen, whether it gets its own chrome-free layout, whether the rest
of the app becomes responsive, offline capture, a native app. Those are separate
conversations to have if and when this one proves itself — not assumptions to
build on.

Explicitly out of scope for this: editing, categorizing, splitting or
reconciling on the phone. Review happens on the desktop app.

## What already works

Worth knowing before building anything, because it shrinks the job:

- **The camera is not the missing capability.** The receipts page input
  (`src/routes/receipts/+page.svelte:607`) is already
  `<input type="file" multiple accept={ACCEPTED_UPLOAD_TYPES}>`, and mobile
  Safari already offers **Take Photo** from it. What is missing is a surface that
  does only that.
- **The image is already handled correctly.** `ReceiptService.uploadAndCreate()`
  resizes to 2400px JPEG, transcodes HEIC, gates on the stored artifact rather
  than the source file, runs OCR fail-soft and cleans up orphaned blobs. A phone
  capture needs none of that rebuilt — see
  [ADR-0006](adr/0006-the-stored-image-is-the-contract.md) and
  [Receipt Image Resize & Zoom](plans-done/2026-08-03-receipt-image-resize-design.md).
- **Batch upload already exists.** `processUploadBatch`
  (`src/lib/utils/batchUpload.ts`) runs files sequentially, independently, so one
  failure doesn't abort the rest.

## Design

One screen with a camera button:

- **A large capture control** using `capture="environment"`, which opens the
  camera directly rather than an intermediate sheet.
- **It calls `uploadAndCreate()`** — the same pipeline as the desktop upload, not
  a second copy of it.
- **Per-file status, visible and retryable.** A failed upload must never be
  silent. A local thumbnail via `URL.createObjectURL` avoids a signed-URL round
  trip.
- **Nothing else on the screen.** No nav, no filters, no table, no totals.

Where it lives is the one open implementation question — see below.

## Open questions

1. **Does this need its own route at all?** A `/capture` route is the obvious
   answer, but it inherits `src/routes/+layout.svelte`'s nav chrome, which is
   most of what makes the receipts page wrong for this. The alternatives are a
   conditional in the existing layout or a route-group split — a real piece of
   work that should be justified by this feature, not assumed by it. Decide after
   trying the simplest version.
2. **What does a phone actually hand over?** Still unverified on-device. HEIC now
   decodes and transcodes to JPEG like everything else, but if Safari's decode
   fails the resize falls back to the original and a large photo is **refused**
   rather than uploaded full-size. This is a live risk in shipped code,
   independent of this feature. Verify before building on it.

## Acceptance criteria

- A photo taken on a phone reaches storage as a resized JPEG and appears as a
  Receipt, via the same pipeline as a desktop upload.
- Taking a second photo does not require waiting for the first to finish.
- A failed upload is visible and can be retried.
- A signed-out user is sent to login and returned afterwards.

-  happens on the desktop app.
-- **Offline capture.** Explicitly deferred to a later phase and constrained by a
-  platform limit (**Risks**). v1 requires a live connection.
-- **Changing the ingestion pipeline.** `uploadAndCreate()` keeps its current
-  semantics — OCR fail-soft, orphan-blob cleanup, `withRetry`. This PRD wraps it,
-  it does not rewrite it. (Moving the pipeline server-side into an Edge Function
-  remains a good idea and a separate decision; it is **not** a prerequisite.)
-- **Android.** The design is standards-based and should work, but iOS Safari is
-  the only target verified.
+- **The camera is not the missing capability.** The receipts page input
+  (`src/routes/receipts/+page.svelte:607`) is already
+  `<input type="file" multiple accept={ACCEPTED_UPLOAD_TYPES}>`, and mobile
+  Safari already offers **Take Photo** from it. What is missing is a surface that
+  does only that.
+- **The image is already handled correctly.** `ReceiptService.uploadAndCreate()`
+  resizes to 2400px JPEG, transcodes HEIC, gates on the stored artifact rather
+  than the source file, runs OCR fail-soft and cleans up orphaned blobs. A phone
+  capture needs none of that rebuilt — see
+  [ADR-0006](adr/0006-the-stored-image-is-the-contract.md) and
+  [Receipt Image Resize & Zoom](plans-done/2026-08-03-receipt-image-resize-design.md).
+- **Batch upload already exists.** `processUploadBatch`
+  (`src/lib/utils/batchUpload.ts`) runs files sequentially, independently, so one
+  failure doesn't abort the rest.
## Design
-### D1 — A PWA route, not a native app (the platform decision)
+One screen with a camera button:
-The existing receipts input (`src/routes/receipts/+page.svelte:489`) is already a
-`<input type="file" accept="image/jpeg,image/png,image/heic,application/pdf"
-multiple>`. On iOS Safari that already offers **Take Photo**, **Photo Library**,
-and **Choose File**. The camera is not the missing capability — the
-single-purpose surface is.
+- **A large capture control** using `capture="environment"`, which opens the
+  camera directly rather than an intermediate sheet.
+- **It calls `uploadAndCreate()`** — the same pipeline as the desktop upload, not
+  a second copy of it.
+- **Per-file status, visible and retryable.** A failed upload must never be
+  silent. A local thumbnail via `URL.createObjectURL` avoids a signed-URL round
+  trip.
+- **Nothing else on the screen.** No nav, no filters, no table, no totals.
-A web app manifest lets one codebase ship two products. With `start_url:
-/capture` and `display: standalone`, the home-screen icon opens chrome-free,
-directly on the capture screen, and never reveals the expenses table or the date
-filters. The desktop app stays at the normal URL.
+Where it lives is the one open implementation question — see below.
-What a native app would add, and why each is insufficient here:
+## Open questions
-| Capability                          | Web            | Native | Verdict for v1 |
-| Camera capture / photo library      | ✅             | ✅     | No gain        |
-| Home-screen icon, standalone chrome | ✅             | ✅     | No gain        |
-| HEIC handling                       | ✅ (**D5**)    | ✅     | No gain        |
-| Share Extension (Photos → app)      | ❌             | ✅     | Real, deferred |
-| Background upload                   | ❌             | ✅     | Real, deferred |
-| Offline queue                       | ❌ (**Risks**) | ✅     | Real, deferred |
-| Document scanner (auto-crop/deskew) | ❌             | ✅     | Real, deferred |
+1. **Does this need its own route at all?** A `/capture` route is the obvious
+   answer, but it inherits `src/routes/+layout.svelte`'s nav chrome, which is
+   most of what makes the receipts page wrong for this. The alternatives are a
+   conditional in the existing layout or a route-group split — a real piece of
+   work that should be justified by this feature, not assumed by it. Decide after
+   trying the simplest version.
+2. **What does a phone actually hand over?** Still unverified on-device. HEIC now
+   decodes and transcodes to JPEG like everything else, but if Safari's decode
+   fails the resize falls back to the original and a large photo is **refused**
+   rather than uploaded full-size. This is a live risk in shipped code,
+   independent of this feature. Verify before building on it.
-Against that: a native app costs an Apple Developer Program membership
-($99/yr), a second toolchain, a second copy of the upload pipeline in Swift — a
-third copy of logic that must stay in lock-step, which is the failure mode
-`CLAUDE.md` already warns about for the Deno `supabase/functions/_shared/`
-duplication — and TestFlight builds that expire every 90 days. The web route
-costs one route and a manifest.
-**Decision: build the web route.** Revisit natively only if the offline scenario
-under **Risks** proves to be a real, recurring need.
-### D2 — Route-group split so the capture screen has no chrome
-`src/routes/+layout.svelte` currently owns three things at once: the auth gate
-(`publicRoutes`, `authChecked`), the nav chrome, and `preserveFilters`. The
-capture screen needs the first and none of the rest.
-Two options:
-- **(a) Route groups.** Move today's layout to `src/routes/(app)/+layout.svelte`
-  and give the capture screen `src/routes/(capture)/+layout.svelte`. Auth
-  handling is lifted into a shared root layout so it is not duplicated. Route
-  groups do not affect URLs, so every existing path is unchanged.
-- **(b) Conditional.** Keep one layout and hide the nav when the path starts with
-  `/capture`.
-**Recommend (a).** Option (b) is one line today and accretes a special case per
-divergence — and this PRD is the first of what will be several: the capture
-screen also wants a different viewport meta, different safe-area padding, and no
-`preserveFilters` subscription. The auth-gate extraction is the only real work;
-it is mechanical and independently testable.
-### D3 — The screen: one shutter, immediate re-arm
-The layout is deliberately impoverished:
-- **A single large shutter control**, thumb-reachable in the lower third, using
-  `capture="environment"` so it opens the camera **directly** — no intermediate
-  sheet.
-- **A smaller secondary control** for the photo library — the same input without
-  the `capture` attribute, so iOS offers the picker.
-- **Immediate re-arm.** Upload starts in the background and the shutter is ready
-  again at once. This is the core interaction: capturing five receipts is five
-  taps.
-- **An upload-queue strip** below the shutter: a local thumbnail per item (from
-  `URL.createObjectURL` — no signed-URL round trip), a state label, and
-  tap-to-retry on failure.
-- **Nothing else.** No nav, no filters, no table, no totals.
-### D4 — The upload queue
-`uploadAndCreate()` today is awaited per file, serially, with the page's
-`uploading` boolean as the only feedback. The capture screen needs per-item state
-and concurrency.
-Each queue item carries: a client-generated id, the local object URL, and one of
-`queued → uploading → extracting → done | failed` (plus the error message for
-`failed`). The mapping onto the existing pipeline is direct — `uploading` covers
-`prepareFileForUpload` + `uploadToStorage`, `extracting` covers
-`extractReceiptDataFailSoft`, `done` is set after
-`insertReceiptOrCleanupUpload` returns.
-Two properties the existing pipeline already gives us and the queue must not
-break: OCR failure still produces a receipt (fail-soft), and a failed insert
-removes the uploaded blob (no orphans). A queue item that reaches `failed`
-therefore has left nothing behind, and retry is safe.
-Concurrency is capped (start at 2) so a burst of captures on cellular does not
-saturate the connection and starve the shot in progress.
-**The queue is presentation state, not business logic.** The state machine and
-the concurrency policy are pure and unit-testable; the Svelte component renders
-them. Do not put upload orchestration inside the component.
-### D5 — HEIC must not bypass the resizer
-`resizeImage()` returns the file untouched for anything that is not JPEG or PNG
-(`src/lib/utils/imageResize.ts:71`), and `prepareFileForUpload()` skips the
-resize call for the same set (`ReceiptService.ts:203`). Meanwhile the receipts
-input opts **into** HEIC via its `accept` list.
-The suspected consequence: iOS Safari transcodes a picked photo to JPEG when the
-`accept` list excludes HEIC, and hands over the original HEIC when it is
-included. If so, today's configuration selects the one path where a full-size
-iPhone photo goes to storage and to Mistral **unresized** — roughly a 3MB upload
-where a 400KB one would do, on the connection least able to afford it. It also
-sits near the 5MB image ceiling in `validateFile()`
-(`ReceiptService.ts:170`), so a large capture can be rejected outright.
-**This is a hypothesis and must be verified on a real device before it is acted
-on** (see **R1**). If confirmed, the capture screen omits `image/heic` from its
-`accept` list so iOS converts to JPEG and the file flows through the existing
-resizer. The desktop receipts page keeps HEIC in its list — a Mac user may
-legitimately upload a `.heic` file, and there the size and bandwidth cost is not
-a concern.
-Note the asymmetry this creates: two `accept` lists for two surfaces, for a
-stated reason. Comment it at both sites.
-### D6 — Installability
-A manifest (`static/manifest.webmanifest`) with `name`, `short_name`,
-`start_url: /capture`, `display: standalone`, theme/background colours, and the
-icon set; plus `apple-touch-icon` and viewport/safe-area meta in `app.html`.
-**No service worker is required for v1.** iOS supports Add to Home Screen and
-honours `display: standalone` from the manifest without one. A service worker is
-introduced only if and when offline persistence (P4) is built — adding one
-earlier buys nothing and brings a cache-invalidation problem the app does not
-currently have.
-## Requirements
-### R1 — Verify the HEIC hypothesis (do this first)
-On a real iPhone, capture through the current receipts input and record: the
-`File.type` and `File.size` the browser hands over, whether `prepareFileForUpload`
-resizes, and the bytes that land in storage. Repeat with `image/heic` removed
-from `accept`. **D5** is contingent on this result; if the behaviour differs from
-the hypothesis, revise D5 rather than implementing it as written.
-### R2 — Layout split
-Per **D2(a)**. Auth gate extracted to a shared root layout; existing nav chrome
-and `preserveFilters` move to `(app)`; a minimal `(capture)` layout. No URL
-changes, no behaviour change to any existing route.
-### R3 — `/capture` route
-Per **D3**. Shutter (`capture="environment"`), library control, queue strip,
-no chrome. Must render correctly with the on-screen keyboard absent and respect
-iOS safe-area insets.
-### R4 — Upload queue
-Per **D4**. Pure state machine + concurrency policy; component renders it.
-Reuses `ReceiptService.uploadAndCreate()` unchanged.
-### R5 — Manifest and icons
-Per **D6**. Installs to the home screen, opens standalone on `/capture`.
-### R6 — Post-capture feedback
-**Open — see Open Questions 1.** The default assumed by this PRD is
-fire-and-forget: the queue strip is the only feedback, plus a passive count of
-receipts awaiting review that deep-links into the desktop app. If inline OCR
-confirmation is chosen instead, R6 grows substantially and P3 should be
-re-estimated.
## Acceptance criteria
-- Tapping the home-screen icon opens the capture screen full-bleed, with no
-  browser or app navigation chrome visible.
-- Tapping the shutter opens the camera directly — no intermediate action sheet.
-- After taking a photo, the shutter is usable again before the upload completes.
-  Five receipts can be captured in five taps without waiting.
-- Each queued item shows a thumbnail and its current state; a failed item shows
-  an error and can be retried, and retrying succeeds once connectivity returns.
-- A receipt captured on the phone appears in the desktop `/expenses` list with
-  the same family scoping, auto-categorisation, and `suspicious_date` behaviour
-  as one uploaded from the desktop. **No divergence in the resulting row.**
-- An image captured on an iPhone arrives in storage resized (≤2000px on the
-  longest axis), whatever format the phone offered.
-- A user who is not signed in is sent to login and returned to `/capture`
-  afterwards — including on first launch in standalone mode.
-- Every existing route renders and behaves exactly as before the layout split.
-## Risks
-- **🔴 Session persistence in standalone mode is the main delivery risk.** An
-  iOS home-screen web app has a storage container separate from Safari, so the
-  user signs in again on first launch inside the installed app. How long that
-  session then survives — across days of non-use, storage pressure, and Safari's
-  storage policies — determines whether this design is pleasant or infuriating.
-  **Spike this during P2, before building anything on top of it.** If sessions
-  prove short-lived, the mitigation (biometric-gated re-auth, longer refresh
-  tokens) is a design change, not a tweak.
-- **🟠 No offline capture on iOS.** Safari does not support the Background Sync
-  API. "Snap five receipts in a parking garage with no signal, pocket the phone,
-  and have them upload later" **does not work on the web**, and no amount of
-  service-worker effort makes it work. The best achievable is holding files in
-  IndexedDB and retrying when the user next opens the app — which requires them
-  to open it. **This is the single scenario that would justify revisiting D1.**
-- **🟠 H3 gets a busier caller.** `/api/ocr/extract` is unauthenticated with no
-  host allow-list on the caller-supplied `fileUrl`. This PRD does not create that
-  hole, but a phone-friendly capture surface will drive materially more traffic
-  through it. Fixing H3 is not a blocker for P1–P2 but should not lag far behind.
-- **🟢 Layout split blast radius.** R2 touches the parent of every route. Low
-  risk, but it is the change most likely to cause a broad regression, which is
-  why it lands on its own (see Sequencing).
-## Testing notes
-Per project convention — unit tests own correctness, Playwright is seam-only:
-- **Unit:** the queue state machine (transitions, retry-after-failure,
-  concurrency cap, ordering) as pure logic with the Supabase client mocked at the
-  boundary. Any `accept`-list or format-selection helper introduced by D5.
-- **Render:** the capture component against a stubbed queue — shutter present and
-  re-armed, per-item states, retry affordance.
-- **Playwright seam:** one thin flow proving the route is wired (file input →
-  `uploadAndCreate` → receipt row), plus a regression pass that existing routes
-  still render after the layout split. Not a device matrix.
-- **Manual, on a real iPhone — unavoidable and not optional.** R1's format
-  investigation, standalone-mode install and session survival, safe-area layout,
-  and the camera-opens-directly behaviour cannot be verified in CI or a
-  simulator. Record the results in this PRD as they are established.
-## Open questions
-1. **Does the capture screen show OCR results, or is it fire-and-forget?** The
-   biggest fork, and it gates R6. OCR takes several seconds via Mistral, so
-   "snap → confirm merchant/amount/date → save" turns a five-second task into a
-   twenty-second one. Fire-and-forget is faster and much simpler, but pushes the
-   `suspicious_date` flag and every OCR miss into a later session on another
-   device — possibly never. **Recommend fire-and-forget for v1**, with a passive
-   "n receipts need review" count. Reverse this if receipts routinely go
-   unreviewed today.
-2. **Route group or conditional nav?** **Recommend the route group (D2a).**
-3. **Is the user willing to install to the home screen?** The design assumes yes.
-   Opening `/capture` in a Safari tab still works but keeps browser chrome and
-   loses the standalone feel — a materially worse product for the same build.
-4. **Multi-shot batching.** Should the library control allow selecting many
-   photos at once (the desktop input already sets `multiple`), or is
-   one-at-a-time the right mobile default? Leaning `multiple` — it costs nothing
-   and the queue already handles n items.
-5. **PDF on mobile.** The desktop accepts PDFs up to 10MB. Does the capture
-   screen offer them at all? Leaning no for v1 — "Choose File" clutters a screen
-   whose entire premise is one tap.
-## Sequencing
-Each phase is independently shippable and leaves the app no worse.
-1. **P1 — R1 (verify HEIC) and R2 (layout split).** Investigation plus the
-   riskiest structural change, landed alone so a regression is unambiguous. No
-   user-visible feature yet.
-2. **P2 — R3 + R4 (the capture screen) and the standalone-session spike.** Usable
-   end-to-end at `/capture` in a browser tab. **Run the session spike before
-   building on top of it.**
-3. **P3 — R5 (manifest, icons) and R6 (feedback, per OQ1).** The point at which
-   it becomes a product rather than a route.
-4. **P4 — queue durability.** IndexedDB persistence so a mid-upload app switch
-   does not lose the shot, plus retry-on-reopen. This is the honest limit of the
-   web platform on iOS; do not promise offline capture beyond it.
-Deferred beyond this PRD: Share Extension, true background upload, and the
-document scanner — all native-only, all revisited together if and only if the
-offline scenario proves real.
+- A photo taken on a phone reaches storage as a resized JPEG and appears as a
+  Receipt, via the same pipeline as a desktop upload.
+- Taking a second photo does not require waiting for the first to finish.
+- A failed upload is visible and can be retried.
+- A signed-out user is sent to login and returned afterwards.

The PRD is back, rewritten from 359 lines to 91. Scope is now literally "take a picture, upload it."

**What went:** the PWA install target, the manifest and icon set, `display: standalone`, the service-worker deferral, the route-group split as a settled decision, the upload-queue state machine, the native-vs-web capability table with its $99/yr costing, and the offline-capture risk assessment. A header note records that they were cut and why, so nobody re-derives them thinking they were an oversight.

**What stayed:** the problem statement — the till, one hand, five seconds — because that's the real reason the receipts page is wrong for this. And a short design: one big `capture="environment"` button, calling the existing `uploadAndCreate()`, per-file status that's visible and retryable, nothing else on screen.

**One section I added that shrinks the job.** "What already works" — the receipts input already offers **Take Photo** in mobile Safari, `uploadAndCreate()` already resizes and transcodes HEIC, and `processUploadBatch` already handles files independently. The camera was never the missing capability; the surface is. Worth knowing before anyone starts building.

**Two open questions, both genuine:**

1. **Does it need its own route at all?** A `/capture` route inherits the nav chrome, which is most of what makes the receipts page wrong here — so it implies a layout split, which is real work. I've written that as something to decide after trying the simplest version, not to assume up front. The old PRD had already picked route groups and called the split "a prerequisite, not a nice-to-have."
2. The on-device HEIC check, which is a live risk in shipped code regardless of this feature.

The backlog line points at the PRD again and names what is *not* decided, so the two documents can't drift back apart.

22	term; pin the final ubiquitous-language name in `domain-model.md` when built.)

27	[Implementation status](#implementation-status),
28	[Spending Chart](#spending-chart-graphical-presentation--built-),

36	## Data model (new)
37	
38	The category hierarchy today is flat: `categories (family_id, name, color)`.
39	There is no Grouping or Importance layer. v1 adds two tiers as real,
40	family-scoped tables so they are first-class and become editable later.
41	
42	- `importance_areas (id, family_id, name, sort_order)` — e.g. Essential
43	  (sort_order 1), Priorities (2), Other (3). The numeric prefix in the sample
44	  (`1. Essential`) becomes `sort_order`, not part of the name.
45	- `category_groups (id, family_id, name, importance_area_id)` — **Importance
46	  attaches to the Grouping**, not to individual categories. Matches the sample
47	  (all of Transportation is Essential) and makes the roll-up a clean two-hop
48	  join. If a future need arises for two categories in one group to have
49	  different importances, revisit — no counterexample in the current sample.
50	- `categories` gains `group_id → category_groups`. A Category belongs to a
51	  Group; the Group carries the Importance.
52	
53	**Seeding.** Derive default Importance areas and Groupings from
54	`docs/SampleHierachy.txt` (cleaned). Map the existing default categories into
55	Groups by name. Near-duplicate categories in the sample (`Car - Insurance` vs
56	`Car insurance`, `Gas` vs `Car - Gas`, `Parking` vs `Car - Parking`) are **not
57	auto-merged** — recognizable names are mapped, the rest fall to Uncategorized.
58	New families are seeded via the same path as `createDefaultCategories`, so any
59	future family gets a working report out of the box.
60	
61	## Report content
62	
63	- **Source:** receipts/Expenses (the app's source of truth for spending), **not**
64	  bank transactions. Bucketed by `transaction_date` (purchase date, not upload
65	  date).
66	- **Currency:** normalized to the family's display currency —
67	  `total_amount × (exchange_rate_to_cad ?? 1)`. CAD for now; the assumption is
68	  isolated so multi-currency drops in later.
69	- **Columns:** January → the last month that has any expense (left edge stays at
70	  January for a stable calendar grid). Interior/empty cells render blank, not
71	  `$0.00`. Final column is labelled **"Year to Date."**
72	- **Rows:** four row types — category detail, **Grouping subtotal**,
73	  **Importance subtotal**, and a final **Grand Total**. Importance ordered by
74	  `sort_order` (Essential → Priorities → Other); Groupings alphabetical within an
75	  Importance; Categories alphabetical within a Grouping. **Zero-activity rows are
76	  suppressed** (a category/group with no spend in the visible window is hidden).
77	- **Uncategorized:** rendered as its own section at the bottom, outside the real
78	  Importance/Grouping subtotals. It **is included in the Grand Total** (and any
79	  month-column totals), so the bottom-right number ties out to the family's
80	  actual total spend. The gap between the three Importance subtotals and the
81	  Grand Total is the deliberate nudge to go categorize.
82	- **Null amounts:** counted as `$0`. No new flag — the receipts and expenses
83	  pages already badge these (`⚠ Amount not read`). At most a small "N receipts
84	  missing an amount" footnote deep-linking to that existing filtered view.

86	## Architecture
87	
88	- **Client-side pure aggregation.** A tested pure function
89	  `buildSpendingReport(expenses, hierarchy, year) → grid`, in the style of the
90	  CSV parsers and date utilities. The small hierarchy tables and the year's
91	  expenses are fetched separately and joined in TypeScript — the existing
92	  expense query is not widened. A family's yearly receipt count is small, so the
93	  data transfer is negligible and the logic stays unit-testable. If volume ever
94	  demands it, swap in a Postgres RPC behind the same function boundary — this
95	  avoids the RLS-fragility minefield the codebase repeatedly warns about.
96	- **Placement:** a new top-level **`/spending`** tab, following the existing
97	  `resolve()` / `filterQuery` nav pattern. May be promoted to the home page
98	  later once proven (currently `/` is "Family Receipts") — a separate change.
99	- **No editing UI in v1.** The hierarchy is hand-maintained (direct SQL) while
100	  the family is a single maintainer. The Uncategorized bucket is the feedback
101	  loop for anything unmapped.

395	## Year-over-year comparison — table columns & bar marker built ✅
396	
397	Now that historical years can be uploaded, the report can show **how spending
398	changed vs. prior years**. This section catalogues the visualization options,
399	then records what shipped first.
400	
401	### The parity rule (load-bearing — governs every option)
402	
403	Every comparison shares one primitive: a **period cutoff** derived from the
404	selected year's own data, applied identically to each comparison year.
405	
406	- **Cutoff = the selected year's last visible month** — the same `maxMonth` the
407	  report already computes for the rightmost ("Year to Date") column. Reused, not
408	  re-derived.
409	- Each comparison year is summed **January → cutoff month only**. A partial 2026
410	  (Jan–Jul) is compared against **Jan–Jul** of the prior year, never its full
411	  Jan–Dec — so a half-finished current year can't lose by construction.
412	- **Whole months only** (the shipped choice). Today being 2026-07-10, July is
413	  partial in 2026 but was complete in 2025; the month-boundary rule compares
414	  Jan–Jul wholesale rather than clipping both to Jul 10. Simpler, matches the
415	  monthly grid, and is what the maintainer asked to start with. A day-boundary
416	  "pace" comparison is possible later (see the cumulative line below) but is not
417	  built.
418	
419	### The options (cheapest → richest)
420	
421	1. **YoY table column** — after "Year to Date", a single **Change** column
422	   (Δ amount + % vs the same Jan→cutoff period last year). Same roll-up levels as
423	   today (category / group / importance / grand total). Pure extension of the
424	   aggregate; no new chart infra. **Built (below)** — a separate Prior-YTD column
425	   was prototyped but dropped as redundant (the change alone carries the signal;
426	   the prior total remains one hover away in the chart tooltip).
427	2. **Prior-period marker on the magnitude bars** — a horizontal tick / ghost line
428	   at each bar's prior-YTD value; the gap between bar top and tick _is_ the
429	   change, read in place with the accordion still working. **Built (below).**
430	3. **Cumulative "pace" line chart** — x = month (Jan → cutoff), y = running
431	   cumulative spend, **one line per year** overlaid, every line stopping at the
432	   same cutoff x so the parity rule is visually self-evident. The natural home
433	   for the month/time story deliberately dropped off the bars. **Deferred.**
434	4. **Diverging change bars** — one bar per Grouping = Δ vs prior YTD, increases
435	   one way / decreases the other, sorted by magnitude; best for _what_ changed.
436	   **Deferred.** (Colour caution: the app already binds red = expense /
437	   green = refund, so a diverging chart must not reuse red/green for
438	   direction — use a neutral diverging pair or encode direction by side + sign.)
439	5. **Waterfall / bridge** — prior-YTD total → one ±step per Grouping →
440	   current-YTD total; decomposes the entire YoY change. Richest, least reuse.
441	   **Built as a horizontal bridge, then ABANDONED as not intuitive** — see
442	   [ADR-0004](../adr/0004-abandon-spending-bridge-waterfall-view.md). Do not
443	   rebuild it; if "what changed, ranked" is wanted, prefer option 4.
444	
445	Deliberately skipped: month×grouping heatmaps and indexed-to-100 growth curves —
446	legible only to spreadsheet-native users, and this report exists to _replace_ the
447	family's manual pivot, not re-create its density.
448	
449	### What shipped (options 1 + 2, pending release; option 5 abandoned)
450	
451	- **Toggle.** A **`Compare {priorYear}`** button in the header (next to
452	  Table | Chart) turns the comparison on/off for **both** views. When the prior
453	  year has **no data**, the toggle still renders but is **disabled** with an
454	  explanatory `title` ("No {priorYear} data to compare"). Effective state is
455	  `comparing = compare && hasPrior`, so stepping the year selector onto a year
456	  whose predecessor has no data silently disables it and re-enables on return.
457	  Comparison is **local page state** (like the Table | Chart toggle), not URL —
458	  it doesn't affect drill-down navigation, so it needn't survive Back.
459	- **Pure core.** `withPriorPeriod(report, priorReport)` in
460	  `src/lib/utils/spendingComparison.ts` attaches `priorYtd` (optional field added
461	  to `ReportRow`) to every row/subtotal/grand-total by summing the prior report's
462	  cells over the first `report.months.length` months (the parity window), matched
463	  by **id** (categoryId / groupId / importanceId) with `(No category)` matched by
464	  name. `spendingChange(current, prior) → { delta, pct, direction }` computes the
465	  Change cell (pct is `null` when prior is 0 → rendered "new"); `hasPriorData`
466	  gates the toggle. Both are unit-tested (`spendingComparison.spec.ts`).
467	- **Table.** A single **Change** column folds into the existing `valueCells`
468	  snippet so every row type gets it; it shows a signed amount + % coloured by
469	  direction (increase / decrease / flat) — no user-facing legend copy. The
470	  Importance/Uncategorized band `colspan`s widen by 1 when comparing. (The
471	  Prior-YTD column was dropped as redundant — see option 1.)
472	- **Chart.** `buildSpendingChart` carries `priorTotal` onto each `ChartBar`
473	  (from the group/category `priorYtd`); `SpendingChart` (new `compare` prop) shows
474	  a **faded prior-year bar side by side** with each current-year bar, and adds the
475	  prior total + change to the hover tooltip. (The bars are drawn as scale-derived
476	  overlays and LayerChart's own bars hidden via `props.bars.opacity`, so current
477	  and prior can sit side by side; the y-domain is sized to the taller of the two
478	  years. Superseded the first cut — a dashed prior-period line — which read as an
479	  ambiguous threshold.) Data loading fetches the prior year's expenses alongside
480	  the current year's (volume is negligible per the aggregate's own design note),
481	  so switching the toggle repaints instantly with no refetch.
482	- **Bridge (option 5) — built, then ABANDONED.** ⚠️ This view was built and pulled
483	  because **users didn't understand it intuitively** — see
484	  [ADR-0004](../adr/0004-abandon-spending-bridge-waterfall-view.md) and the
485	  reminder screenshot [`docs/BridgeChartTooWide.png`](../BridgeChartTooWide.png).
486	  The description below is kept as a record of what was tried; the code
487	  (`SpendingBridge.svelte`, `spendingWaterfall.ts`, their specs, and the `Bridge`
488	  toggle) has been **removed**. **Do not rebuild it.** A **horizontal waterfall**
489	  with the **areas on the Y-axis** and the running cumulative amount on the
490	  X-axis: the top anchor is the prior-year same-period grand total, one floating
491	  step per area (up = spent more / down = spent less, same red/green as the Change
492	  column), the bottom anchor is the current-year grand total — the steps always
493	  reconcile.
494	  - **Pure core** `buildWaterfallBridge(current, prior, expandedGroups)` in
495	    `src/lib/utils/spendingWaterfall.ts`. Unlike the magnitude chart it reads
496	    **both** reports and walks the **union** of groups/categories across the two
497	    years, so a **disappeared** area (spent last year, nothing this year — no
498	    current row) still appears as its own downward step. Prior totals use the same
499	    whole-month parity window. Reconciliation holds at every level: Σ step deltas =
500	    current − prior grand total. 10 unit tests (`spendingWaterfall.spec.ts`).
501	  - **Accordion preserved.** Expanding a Grouping emits a **header row** (which
502	    keeps the − collapse toggle and shows the group's net change at 40 % opacity)
503	    followed by its Category steps in place; because the category deltas sum to the
504	    group delta, the running total on either side is unchanged. Many open at once
505	    (`SvelteSet`), like the magnitude chart.
506	  - **Rendering** is a self-contained `SpendingBridge.svelte` — percentage-scaled
507	    off the model's running-total domain (no width measurement, resizes for free),
508	    Importance colour on the row's left border + a legend, hover tooltip with
509	    current / prior / change. Only reachable when the prior year has data (the
510	    `Bridge` toggle is disabled otherwise). 3 render tests.
511	
512	**Known limitations (documented, not bugs).**
513	
514	- **Disappeared spend is invisible in the table & chart.** The Change column and
515	  the side-by-side prior bar both hang off the _current_ report's rows, so a
516	  Grouping/Category that had spend last year but none this year has no row/bar to
517	  annotate. The Grand-Total row still reflects it. (The abandoned Bridge view
518	  surfaced it as a downward step — the one thing only that view did; if it's
519	  wanted again, build **diverging change bars**, not a waterfall. See
520	  [ADR-0004](../adr/0004-abandon-spending-bridge-waterfall-view.md).)
521	- **Whole-month only** (see the parity rule) — the current partial month is
522	  compared against the prior year's _full_ same month.
523	
524	## Deferred (later slices)
525	
526	- ~~Prior-period overlay line + year-over-year comparison~~ — **built ✅** (a table
527	  Change column + a prior-period bar marker; pending release), see
528	  [Year-over-year comparison](#year-over-year-comparison--table-columns--bar-marker-built-).
529	  A third **Bridge / waterfall** view was built and **abandoned as not intuitive**
530	  ([ADR-0004](../adr/0004-abandon-spending-bridge-waterfall-view.md)). Richer YoY
531	  views remain deferred: **cumulative pace line**, **diverging change bars**.
532	- ~~Historical-year expense upload~~ — **built ✅** (pending release), see section above.
533	- Arbitrary period / quarter selection (beyond a single calendar year).
534	- The multi-chart-type menu and any second chart type (trend, magnitude).
535	- Hierarchy tier CRUD — mostly built (assign + re-parent, and now **add/rename
536	  Groupings**, v0.67). **Importance-area CRUD is a permanent non-goal** — the 3
537	  seeded areas are fixed and will not change. Not built (but possible later):
538	  **Grouping delete** (empty groups are inert) and **Grouping reorder**
539	  (`sort_order`). See the Editable-hierarchy section above.
540	- Export (CSV / PDF).
541	- Promoting the report to the home page.
542	
543	## Known limitations (document when building)
544	
545	- **Refunds.** Refunds are represented as **negative `total_amount`** on a
546	  receipt (confirmed via `formatCurrency.spec.ts` and the export services). The
547	  report **keeps the sign**, so refunds net against spend — which is the correct
548	  behaviour for a spending total. (Note the CSV/PDF _exporters_ deliberately
549	  `abs()` refunds; the report does not.) One visible consequence: a Category or
550	  Grouping whose refunds exceed its spend in the window shows a **negative**
551	  total — informative, not a bug. No special handling needed in v1; documented
552	  here so the divergence from the exporters is intentional and searchable.
553	- **"Year to Date" label** reads oddly for a _completed past_ year (it is the
554	  full-year total). Relabel per-context when the multi-year slice lands. Not a
555	  v1 problem since v1 is current-year only.
556
