# Spending Report Design

**Date:** 2026-07-09
**Status:** ✅ Built — table + chart views, cell drill-down, hierarchy editing
(assign categories to groups, re-parent groups, add & rename Groupings),
**historical-year expense upload from CSV/Excel**, and **year-over-year
comparison** (a Change column on the table + side-by-side prior-year bars on the
chart) are all shipped and live. A third comparison view — a horizontal **Bridge /
waterfall** — was built and then **abandoned as not intuitive** and **removed**; see
[ADR-0004](../adr/0004-abandon-spending-bridge-waterfall-view.md). Remaining work
is the
[Deferred](#deferred-later-slices) slices (richer YoY views — cumulative pace
line, diverging change bars — plus period selection and export).
Grouping tier editing is built; what's left of "tier CRUD" is deliberately out of
scope (fixed Importance areas, no Grouping delete/reorder).

## Overview

A top-level **Spending** report that rolls up Expenses by **Importance →
Grouping → Category** across the months of a year. It replaces the Excel pivot
table the family currently maintains by hand. ("Spending Report" is the working
term; pin the final ubiquitous-language name in `domain-model.md` when built.)

Built ✅: the **table view** (v1), the **chart view** (an accordion magnitude bar
chart), **cell drill-down** into the Expenses view, and **hierarchy editing**
(assign categories to groups, re-parent groups, assign-on-create) — see
[Implementation status](#implementation-status),
[Spending Chart](#spending-chart-graphical-presentation--built-),
[Drill-down](#drill-from-a-table-cell-into-the-expenses-view--built-), and
[Editable hierarchy](#editable-hierarchy--assign--re-parent--built-). Year-over-year
comparison (a table Change column + chart marker) is also built (see
[Year-over-year comparison](#year-over-year-comparison--table-columns--bar-marker-built-)).
Still deferred: selectable periods, richer YoY views (pace line / diverging),
tier CRUD, and export (see [Deferred](#deferred-later-slices)).

## Data model (new)

The category hierarchy today is flat: `categories (family_id, name, color)`.
There is no Grouping or Importance layer. v1 adds two tiers as real,
family-scoped tables so they are first-class and become editable later.

- `importance_areas (id, family_id, name, sort_order)` — e.g. Essential
  (sort_order 1), Priorities (2), Other (3). The numeric prefix in the sample
  (`1. Essential`) becomes `sort_order`, not part of the name.
- `category_groups (id, family_id, name, importance_area_id)` — **Importance
  attaches to the Grouping**, not to individual categories. Matches the sample
  (all of Transportation is Essential) and makes the roll-up a clean two-hop
  join. If a future need arises for two categories in one group to have
  different importances, revisit — no counterexample in the current sample.
- `categories` gains `group_id → category_groups`. A Category belongs to a
  Group; the Group carries the Importance.

**Seeding.** Derive default Importance areas and Groupings from
`docs/SampleHierachy.txt` (cleaned). Map the existing default categories into
Groups by name. Near-duplicate categories in the sample (`Car - Insurance` vs
`Car insurance`, `Gas` vs `Car - Gas`, `Parking` vs `Car - Parking`) are **not
auto-merged** — recognizable names are mapped, the rest fall to Uncategorized.
New families are seeded via the same path as `createDefaultCategories`, so any
future family gets a working report out of the box.

## Report content

- **Source:** receipts/Expenses (the app's source of truth for spending), **not**
  bank transactions. Bucketed by `transaction_date` (purchase date, not upload
  date).
- **Currency:** normalized to the family's display currency —
  `total_amount × (exchange_rate_to_cad ?? 1)`. CAD for now; the assumption is
  isolated so multi-currency drops in later.
- **Columns:** January → the last month that has any expense (left edge stays at
  January for a stable calendar grid). Interior/empty cells render blank, not
  `$0.00`. Final column is labelled **"Year to Date."**
- **Rows:** four row types — category detail, **Grouping subtotal**,
  **Importance subtotal**, and a final **Grand Total**. Importance ordered by
  `sort_order` (Essential → Priorities → Other); Groupings alphabetical within an
  Importance; Categories alphabetical within a Grouping. **Zero-activity rows are
  suppressed** (a category/group with no spend in the visible window is hidden).
- **Uncategorized:** rendered as its own section at the bottom, outside the real
  Importance/Grouping subtotals. It **is included in the Grand Total** (and any
  month-column totals), so the bottom-right number ties out to the family's
  actual total spend. The gap between the three Importance subtotals and the
  Grand Total is the deliberate nudge to go categorize.
- **Null amounts:** counted as `$0`. No new flag — the receipts and expenses
  pages already badge these (`⚠ Amount not read`). At most a small "N receipts
  missing an amount" footnote deep-linking to that existing filtered view.

## Architecture

- **Client-side pure aggregation.** A tested pure function
  `buildSpendingReport(expenses, hierarchy, year) → grid`, in the style of the
  CSV parsers and date utilities. The small hierarchy tables and the year's
  expenses are fetched separately and joined in TypeScript — the existing
  expense query is not widened. A family's yearly receipt count is small, so the
  data transfer is negligible and the logic stays unit-testable. If volume ever
  demands it, swap in a Postgres RPC behind the same function boundary — this
  avoids the RLS-fragility minefield the codebase repeatedly warns about.
- **Placement:** a new top-level **`/spending`** tab, following the existing
  `resolve()` / `filterQuery` nav pattern. May be promoted to the home page
  later once proven (currently `/` is "Family Receipts") — a separate change.
- **No editing UI in v1.** The hierarchy is hand-maintained (direct SQL) while
  the family is a single maintainer. The Uncategorized bucket is the feedback
  loop for anything unmapped.

## Implementation status ✅

v1 is built and running against live data (v0.50). What landed:

- **Migration** `supabase/migrations/20260709_spending_hierarchy.sql` — creates
  `importance_areas` and `category_groups`, adds `categories.group_id`
  (`ON DELETE SET NULL`), family-scoped RLS mirroring `categories_family_access`,
  unique-per-family name indexes, and `updated_at` triggers. Ships
  `create_default_hierarchy(p_family_id)` (idempotent, `SECURITY DEFINER`): seeds
  3 Importance areas + 13 Groupings and maps categories → groups by name (a
  superset covering both the current default names and the older spreadsheet
  names). Backfills every existing family in a `DO` loop; the app calls it via
  RPC for new families.
- **Grouping → Importance seed choices.** Each Grouping is collapsed to a single
  Importance (the model attaches Importance to the Grouping): **Essential** =
  Everyday, Health, Home, Transportation, Income Taxes; **Priorities** = Banking
  & Investing, Debt, Fitness, Kids, Rental; **Other** = Discretionary, Gifts,
  Travel. Where the source spreadsheet split a Grouping across importances (e.g.
  Home's Garden/Household goods were "Other"), it now rolls up under the
  Grouping's single Importance. Change with a one-row `UPDATE` on
  `category_groups.importance_area_id`.
- **Aggregation** `src/lib/utils/spendingReport.ts` — the pure
  `buildSpendingReport(expenses, categories, groups, importanceAreas, year)`.
  21 unit tests in `spendingReport.spec.ts` (month columns, roll-up/subtotals,
  ordering, Uncategorized, refund netting, FX, null amounts, blank-vs-zero cells).
  Per-cell `{ amount, count }` drives blank (count 0) vs `0.00` (net-zero but had
  activity).
- **Types** `src/lib/types/Hierarchy.ts` (`ImportanceArea`, `CategoryGroup`);
  `Category` gains `group_id`.
- **Service** `CategoryService` gains `getFamilyImportanceAreas`,
  `getFamilyGroups`, and `createDefaultHierarchy` (RPC wrapper).
- **Page + nav** `src/routes/spending/+page.svelte` + a **Spending** top-level
  tab. Self-seeds the hierarchy on first open (mirrors default-categories
  lazy-init), then loads hierarchy + the year's expenses and paints the grid.
  Year prev/next selector, missing-amount footnote, Importance bands, Grouping
  and Importance subtotals, Uncategorized section, Grand Total. The **selected
  year lives in the URL** (`/spending?year=2025`) and is read in a **`+page.ts`
  `load`** (pure `parseYearParam`); the page consumes `data.year`, and the year
  arrows `goto('?year=…', { replaceState: true })`. A reload `$effect` fires when
  `data.year` (or the resolved family) changes. `load` is the single source of
  truth: SvelteKit re-runs it with the correct URL on every navigation — arrows,
  a refresh, and **Back from a cell drill-down** — so it never snaps back to the
  current year (which would show an empty grid for a data-only-in-2025 family).
  Three client-side attempts failed first and are recorded so they aren't retried:
  (1) read-once-in-`onMount` raced the initial render; (2) `$derived` off the
  legacy `$app/stores` `$page` store went stale on Back; (3) `$derived` off the
  `$app/state` reactive `page` _plus_ `replaceState`-driven arrows still went
  stale on Back and left the arrows inert. The `load` approach is the robust fix.
  Fix pending release (version assigned on commit).
- **Rendering details.** Long category names truncate to one line
  (`max-w-64 truncate`) with the full name on hover via `title`. The layout gives
  `/spending` full window width (`max-w-full`); other pages keep `max-w-5xl`.

**Verification:** `npm run check`, `eslint`, and Prettier clean on touched files;
full unit suite green (1278 passed / 8 skipped, incl. the 21 new). Production
build succeeds. Not yet exercised: a rendered end-to-end pass (no local
auth/seed harness) — validated live by the maintainer instead.

**Known open item surfaced by live data:** the seed maps by name, so any custom
or renamed category lands in Uncategorized until its `group_id` is set by hand.

## Spending Chart (graphical presentation) — built ✅

A `Table | Chart` toggle on `/spending` (shared year selector + loaded data)
adds a **magnitude bar chart** view (v0.60).

> **Design note — why not stacked-by-month.** The first cut stacked 12 month
> segments per bar with a sequential ramp. In real data it failed twice: the 12
> subtle shades read as noise ("the gradient is a mess"), and one dominant
> Grouping (a family's ~$33k Home, driven by a one-off $20k renovation) crushed
> every other bar's height so small bars were unreadable. Both flaws trace to the
> month stack. v0.60 drops it: **solid magnitude bars + value labels**, with the
> month/time story deferred to the separate trend chart.

- **Form:** one **solid bar per Grouping** = its year-to-date total, **coloured by
  Area of Importance** (a validated 3-colour categorical palette: Essential
  `#4f46e5`, Priorities `#0d9488`, Other `#d97706`; Uncategorized neutral gray).
  Bars ordered by Importance `sort_order` then Grouping name; **Uncategorized**
  trails; zero-activity groups suppressed.
- **Value label** above every bar (formatted currency), so a tiny bar next to a
  dominant one is still readable — the fix for the outlier problem without a
  scale hack. Positioned from the bound LayerChart `context` (band x-scale +
  linear y-scale).
- **Two bracket rows beneath the axis** carry the hierarchy, both positioned from
  the bound `context` band x-scale (aligned on resize):
  - **Row 1 — Grouping ± toggles.** One keyboard-focusable `<button>` bracket per
    Grouping, spanning its bar(s), showing `+ Name` / `− Name`. This is the
    expand/collapse control (see interaction) and the Grouping label.
  - **Row 2 — Area of Importance**, labelled **once per contiguous run** of
    same-Importance bars, in that Importance's colour. Uncategorized has no
    Importance bracket (its Grouping bracket names it).
- **Interaction: expand in place (accordion), not drill-and-replace.** Clicking a
  Grouping's bar **or** its ± bracket expands it into its **Category** bars _in
  place_ while its siblings stay visible; **any number of Groupings can be open at
  once** (`expandedGroups` is a reactive `SvelteSet`). Expanded Categories keep the
  parent Grouping's Importance colour and sit inside the same Importance bracket.
  Bars are keyed by a unique id, not name, so same-named Categories across
  Groupings don't collide on the band scale.
- **Click + hover come from a custom per-bar overlay, not LayerChart.** LayerChart's
  own tooltip layer both swallows bar clicks and can't carry a month breakdown, so
  `tooltipContext` is disabled and a transparent full-height column is drawn over
  each bar (from the band scale). It handles the click (toggle its Grouping) and the
  hover, which shows a **tooltip with the bar's name, its per-month totals, and the
  grand total** — the monthly detail dropped from the bars themselves. The overlay
  columns are `aria-hidden`/non-focusable mouse affordances; the ± brackets remain
  the keyboard-accessible controls.
- **Long labels don't collide.** When a Grouping expands into many Category bars,
  each axis label is truncated to one bar width with an ellipsis (`Meals and Drinks
Out` → `Meals…`); the full name is in the hover tooltip. Collapsed Grouping names
  live in their ± bracket (truncated there too). The one-line usage hint sits below
  the chart.
- **Data:** no new aggregation — the pure
  `buildSpendingChart(report, expandedGroups)` reshapes the existing
  `SpendingReport` into a flat `{ months, bars }` where expanded Groupings
  contribute their Category bars in place (unit-tested in `spendingChart.spec.ts`).
  The per-bar `monthly` map is retained for the future trend chart / hover detail;
  the current view uses only `total`.
- **Library:** **LayerChart 2.0.1** (`<BarChart>` with `y="total"` and a `c`
  ordinal colour scale by Importance; `bandPadding`, rounded bars). Peer
  `svelte@^5`. Its built-in tooltip/click layer (`tooltipContext`) is **disabled**
  in favour of the custom overlay above. Colours validated with the dataviz palette
  script (CVD ΔE 57.8, contrast ≥ 3:1); identity carried by position + brackets,
  not colour alone.
- **Verification:** `SpendingChart.svelte.spec.ts` (8 tests) renders it in Chromium
  and asserts: a bar per Grouping lays out, the once-only Importance brackets, the
  per-bar value labels, expand-in-place (siblings stay), several open at once,
  collapse back, **the bar itself (not just the bracket) expands**, and **the hover
  tooltip shows name + month totals + grand total**. `spendingChart.spec.ts`
  (6 tests) covers the pure accordion model; `spendingReport.spec.ts` (21) the
  aggregation.

**Chart known limitation:**

- **Prior-period comparison** (a **faded prior-year bar side by side** with each
  current-year bar) is now **built** behind the `Compare` toggle — see
  [Year-over-year comparison](#year-over-year-comparison--table-columns--bar-marker-built-).
  Month-by-month detail still lives in the Table view and the hover tooltip; a
  dedicated cumulative-pace trend chart remains the natural home for it (deferred).

## Drill from a table cell into the Expenses view — built ✅

The table's numbers are a jumping-off point (v0.55): clicking a non-blank cell
navigates to the **Expenses** view, filtered to exactly the Expenses that
produced that number.

- **Category detail cell** (category × month) → that **category** in that
  **month**. **Category "Year to Date" cell** → that category across the year.
- **Subtotal cells** roll the filter up to match what they sum:
  - **Grouping subtotal** → every category id in that Grouping (that month/YTD).
  - **Importance subtotal** → every category id across the Importance's groups.
  - **Grand Total** → the date range alone (no category filter) so it ties out to
    all Expenses, **including Uncategorized**.
  - **Uncategorized** cells → the `filter=uncategorized` Expenses filter. A
    named-but-ungrouped category row instead drills to its own category id
    (precise); only the section subtotal and the "(No category)" row use the
    coarse `filter=uncategorized` (which by design covers only null-category
    Expenses, so a subtotal with ungrouped-category rows is a slight over-scope).
- **What shipped.**
  - **Pure** `buildSpendingDrilldownParams(scope, column, year, categories, groups)`
    → `URLSearchParams` in `src/lib/utils/spendingDrilldown.ts`; the scope
    (category / group / importance / uncategorized / grandTotal) and column
    (a month or YTD) come from the clicked row. 8 unit tests in
    `spendingDrilldown.spec.ts`.
  - **Report identity.** `buildSpendingReport` rows/sections now carry the ids the
    drill-down needs: `ReportRow.categoryId`, `GroupSection.id`,
    `ImportanceSection.id` (additive; 6 new tests, 27 total in
    `spendingReport.spec.ts`).
  - **Page.** `/spending` table cells render as `<a href>` links to `/expenses?…`;
    **blank cells (count 0) are not links**.
- **Real Expenses-page contract** (corrects the earlier guess): the params are
  **`dateFrom`/`dateTo`** (inclusive `YYYY-MM-DD`, via `readDateFilter`), category
  is **`category=id,id`**, and uncategorized is **`filter=uncategorized`** — which
  takes precedence over `category`, so the two are never set together.
- **Not yet:** the same affordance on chart bars (deferred). Verified live by the
  maintainer (no auth/seed harness for an end-to-end render pass), like v1.

## Editable hierarchy — assign & re-parent — built ✅

An **Edit hierarchy** page at **`/spending/hierarchy`** (linked from a button on
`/spending`) lets the maintainer restructure the hierarchy without SQL (v0.65).
This directly closes the "Known open item" above: custom/renamed categories that
the name-based seed left in Uncategorized can now be pulled into a Grouping in
the UI.

- **Two mutations shipped** (the highest-value slice):
  - **Assign a Category to a Grouping** (or back to Uncategorized) — a per-category
    `<select>` grouped by Importance via `<optgroup>`.
    `CategoryService.assignCategoryToGroup(categoryId, groupId | null)`.
  - **Move a Grouping to another Area of Importance** — a per-group `<select>`.
    Because Importance attaches to the Grouping, this re-buckets all the group's
    categories at once. `CategoryService.moveGroupToImportance(groupId, importanceAreaId)`.
- **Unassigned bucket up top.** Categories with no `group_id` render in an amber
  "Unassigned categories (N)" section — the editor's whole reason to exist — each
  with the same group picker. Below it, the full Importance → Grouping → Category
  tree with **zero-activity rows NOT suppressed** (unlike the report; every group
  and category must be assignable).
- **Architecture mirrors the report.** Pure `buildHierarchyTree(importanceAreas,
groups, categories) → { importances, unassigned }` in
  `src/lib/utils/hierarchyTree.ts` shapes the three flat tables into the nested
  tree (Importance by `sort_order`, Groupings/Categories alphabetical; orphan
  groups whose Importance FK doesn't resolve fold into a trailing synthetic node
  so nothing is silently dropped). Presentation is a pure
  `HierarchyEditor.svelte` (props in, `onAssignCategory`/`onMoveGroup` out); the
  page owns loading + the CategoryService calls and reloads after each mutation.
  The page self-seeds the hierarchy if empty, like `/spending`.
- **Verification.** `hierarchyTree.spec.ts` (8, pure tree) +
  `HierarchyEditor.svelte.spec.ts` (5, renders the bucket/sections and asserts the
  selects emit the right ids incl. assign-to-null). `check`/eslint/Prettier clean;
  full suite green; production build succeeds. Live end-to-end pass by the
  maintainer (no auth/seed harness), like the earlier slices.

- **Assign-on-create (v0.66).** The inline "Create new category…" form in
  `CategoryDropdown` (expenses page) now offers an optional **Group** selector, so
  a category can be filed into a Grouping at birth instead of landing in
  Uncategorized. `CategoryService.createCategory` gained an optional 4th `groupId`
  arg; the expenses page loads the family's Groupings and passes them in. The
  selector is hidden when no Groupings are supplied, so the receipt/reconciliation
  uses of `CategoryDropdown` (which don't pass `groups`) are unchanged. Tests: 3
  new in `CategoryDropdown.svelte.spec.ts`, 2 in `CategoryService.spec.ts`.

- **Add & rename Groupings (v0.67).** The editor now creates new Groupings and
  renames existing ones, so the tier is no longer SQL-only. An **"Add a Grouping"**
  form (name + Area of Importance) sits below the tree
  (`CategoryService.createGroup(familyId, name, importanceAreaId)`); the new empty
  group appears in its area, ready to have categories assigned into it. Each
  Grouping header has an inline **Rename** (`CategoryService.renameGroup(groupId,
name)`) — safe because the report and editor key off the group id, not its name.
  Both service methods validate the name and map the unique-per-family `23505`
  violation to a friendly message. Tests: 4 new in `CategoryService.spec.ts`
  (create + rename, validation, duplicate-name), 3 in
  `HierarchyEditor.svelte.spec.ts` (add emits name+area, add stays disabled until
  both set, rename emits the edited name).

**Out of scope — the Importance tier is fixed, permanently.** The 3 seeded areas
(Essential / Priorities / Other) will **not** change: there is no add/rename/
reorder UI and none is planned — this is a settled product decision, not a
deferral. Treat Importance-area CRUD as a non-goal.

**Still deferred (Groupings):** Groupings have **no delete** — an empty Grouping
is inert since the report suppresses zero-activity rows, so deleting it (and the
delete-confirmation it would need) buys nothing. Grouping `sort_order` reorder is
also unbuilt (Groupings render alphabetically). Revisit only if a real need
appears.

## Historical-year expense upload — built ✅

A **Import Expenses** page at **`/expenses/import`** (buttons on both `/expenses`
and `/spending`) imports historical Expenses from a CSV / XLS / XLSX file
(pending release — version assigned on commit). This is the keystone of the
year-over-year thread: it's the only way to
get prior years' Expenses into the app so the deferred prior-period overlay /
YoY slices have data to compare against.

- **File format.** Columns `Timestamp, Merchant, Amount, Category` (a `Tag`
  column is parsed-and-dropped — there is no tag concept in the schema). `Amount`
  keeps its sign: **positive = expense, negative = refund**, the same convention
  as `receipts.total_amount`, so refunds net against spend exactly as real
  receipts do (no inversion, no `abs()`). `Category` is a plain name; blank →
  Uncategorized.
- **Each row becomes an imageless receipt + a category link.** No schema change
  was needed: `receipts.receipt_image_path` is nullable and `createManual`
  already creates receipts with no image and `suspicious_date` forced `false`
  (these are intentional old entries). A row is one `receipts` insert plus, when
  it has a category, one `expense_categories` upsert (`source: 'manual'`).
  Category names resolve against the family's categories case-insensitively;
  genuinely new names are **created** and land in Uncategorized until filed in
  the hierarchy editor.
- **Two-step preview → confirm.** Unlike the transaction importer (which commits
  straight to the DB), this shows a preview first: how many expenses will import,
  how many duplicates will be skipped, which new categories will be created (with
  a warning + link to the hierarchy editor), and any unreadable rows. Nothing is
  written until the maintainer confirms.
- **Re-import is safe (count-based dedup).** `computeExpenseImportPlan` keys on
  `date | merchant | amount | category` and inserts only `max(0, fileCount −
dbCount)` per key, scoping the existing-rows query to the file's date range —
  re-running the same file is a no-op.
- **Architecture mirrors the report** (pure core + imperative shell). Pure:
  `parseExpenseImportCsv` (`src/lib/utils/expenseImportCsv.ts`),
  `computeExpenseImportPlan` + `buildExpenseCategoryLinks`
  (`src/lib/utils/expenseImportPlan.ts`). Shell: `ExpenseImportService`
  (`buildPreview`/`previewFromText` → `commit`). Reuse: the bank-parser CSV
  primitives (tokenizer, date, amount) were **extracted** from `BaseCSVParser`
  into `src/lib/utils/csvPrimitives.ts` (base now delegates; the 7 bank-parser
  suites are the oracle) so the tokenizer isn't duplicated; `ExcelToCSVConverter`
  handles XLS/XLSX.
- **Verification.** 14 tests `expenseImportCsv.spec.ts`, 12
  `expenseImportPlan.spec.ts`, 7 `ExpenseImportService.spec.ts` (a purpose-built
  Supabase fake dispatching by table/op). `check`/eslint/Prettier clean; full
  suite green; the 229 bank-parser tests still pass after the primitive
  extraction. Live end-to-end pass by the maintainer (no auth/seed harness), like
  the earlier slices.

## Year-over-year comparison — table columns & bar marker built ✅

Now that historical years can be uploaded, the report can show **how spending
changed vs. prior years**. This section catalogues the visualization options,
then records what shipped first.

### The parity rule (load-bearing — governs every option)

Every comparison shares one primitive: a **period cutoff** derived from the
selected year's own data, applied identically to each comparison year.

- **Cutoff = the selected year's last visible month** — the same `maxMonth` the
  report already computes for the rightmost ("Year to Date") column. Reused, not
  re-derived.
- Each comparison year is summed **January → cutoff month only**. A partial 2026
  (Jan–Jul) is compared against **Jan–Jul** of the prior year, never its full
  Jan–Dec — so a half-finished current year can't lose by construction.
- **Whole months only** (the shipped choice). Today being 2026-07-10, July is
  partial in 2026 but was complete in 2025; the month-boundary rule compares
  Jan–Jul wholesale rather than clipping both to Jul 10. Simpler, matches the
  monthly grid, and is what the maintainer asked to start with. A day-boundary
  "pace" comparison is possible later (see the cumulative line below) but is not
  built.

### The options (cheapest → richest)

1. **YoY table column** — after "Year to Date", a single **Change** column
   (Δ amount + % vs the same Jan→cutoff period last year). Same roll-up levels as
   today (category / group / importance / grand total). Pure extension of the
   aggregate; no new chart infra. **Built (below)** — a separate Prior-YTD column
   was prototyped but dropped as redundant (the change alone carries the signal;
   the prior total remains one hover away in the chart tooltip).
2. **Prior-period marker on the magnitude bars** — a horizontal tick / ghost line
   at each bar's prior-YTD value; the gap between bar top and tick _is_ the
   change, read in place with the accordion still working. **Built (below).**
3. **Cumulative "pace" line chart** — x = month (Jan → cutoff), y = running
   cumulative spend, **one line per year** overlaid, every line stopping at the
   same cutoff x so the parity rule is visually self-evident. The natural home
   for the month/time story deliberately dropped off the bars. **Deferred.**
4. **Diverging change bars** — one bar per Grouping = Δ vs prior YTD, increases
   one way / decreases the other, sorted by magnitude; best for _what_ changed.
   **Deferred.** (Colour caution: the app already binds red = expense /
   green = refund, so a diverging chart must not reuse red/green for
   direction — use a neutral diverging pair or encode direction by side + sign.)
5. **Waterfall / bridge** — prior-YTD total → one ±step per Grouping →
   current-YTD total; decomposes the entire YoY change. Richest, least reuse.
   **Built as a horizontal bridge, then ABANDONED as not intuitive** — see
   [ADR-0004](../adr/0004-abandon-spending-bridge-waterfall-view.md). Do not
   rebuild it; if "what changed, ranked" is wanted, prefer option 4.

Deliberately skipped: month×grouping heatmaps and indexed-to-100 growth curves —
legible only to spreadsheet-native users, and this report exists to _replace_ the
family's manual pivot, not re-create its density.

### What shipped (options 1 + 2, pending release; option 5 abandoned)

- **Toggle.** A **`Compare {priorYear}`** button in the header (next to
  Table | Chart) turns the comparison on/off for **both** views. When the prior
  year has **no data**, the toggle still renders but is **disabled** with an
  explanatory `title` ("No {priorYear} data to compare"). Effective state is
  `comparing = compare && hasPrior`, so stepping the year selector onto a year
  whose predecessor has no data silently disables it and re-enables on return.
  Comparison is **local page state** (like the Table | Chart toggle), not URL —
  it doesn't affect drill-down navigation, so it needn't survive Back.
- **Pure core.** `withPriorPeriod(report, priorReport)` in
  `src/lib/utils/spendingComparison.ts` attaches `priorYtd` (optional field added
  to `ReportRow`) to every row/subtotal/grand-total by summing the prior report's
  cells over the first `report.months.length` months (the parity window), matched
  by **id** (categoryId / groupId / importanceId) with `(No category)` matched by
  name. `spendingChange(current, prior) → { delta, pct, direction }` computes the
  Change cell (pct is `null` when prior is 0 → rendered "new"); `hasPriorData`
  gates the toggle. Both are unit-tested (`spendingComparison.spec.ts`).
- **Table.** A single **Change** column folds into the existing `valueCells`
  snippet so every row type gets it; it shows a signed amount + % coloured by
  direction (increase / decrease / flat) — no user-facing legend copy. The
  Importance/Uncategorized band `colspan`s widen by 1 when comparing. (The
  Prior-YTD column was dropped as redundant — see option 1.)
- **Chart.** `buildSpendingChart` carries `priorTotal` onto each `ChartBar`
  (from the group/category `priorYtd`); `SpendingChart` (new `compare` prop) shows
  a **faded prior-year bar side by side** with each current-year bar, and adds the
  prior total + change to the hover tooltip. (The bars are drawn as scale-derived
  overlays and LayerChart's own bars hidden via `props.bars.opacity`, so current
  and prior can sit side by side; the y-domain is sized to the taller of the two
  years. Superseded the first cut — a dashed prior-period line — which read as an
  ambiguous threshold.) Data loading fetches the prior year's expenses alongside
  the current year's (volume is negligible per the aggregate's own design note),
  so switching the toggle repaints instantly with no refetch.
- **Bridge (option 5) — built, then ABANDONED.** ⚠️ This view was built and pulled
  because **users didn't understand it intuitively** — see
  [ADR-0004](../adr/0004-abandon-spending-bridge-waterfall-view.md) and the
  reminder screenshot [`docs/BridgeChartTooWide.png`](../BridgeChartTooWide.png).
  The description below is kept as a record of what was tried; the code
  (`SpendingBridge.svelte`, `spendingWaterfall.ts`, their specs, and the `Bridge`
  toggle) has been **removed**. **Do not rebuild it.** A **horizontal waterfall**
  with the **areas on the Y-axis** and the running cumulative amount on the
  X-axis: the top anchor is the prior-year same-period grand total, one floating
  step per area (up = spent more / down = spent less, same red/green as the Change
  column), the bottom anchor is the current-year grand total — the steps always
  reconcile.
  - **Pure core** `buildWaterfallBridge(current, prior, expandedGroups)` in
    `src/lib/utils/spendingWaterfall.ts`. Unlike the magnitude chart it reads
    **both** reports and walks the **union** of groups/categories across the two
    years, so a **disappeared** area (spent last year, nothing this year — no
    current row) still appears as its own downward step. Prior totals use the same
    whole-month parity window. Reconciliation holds at every level: Σ step deltas =
    current − prior grand total. 10 unit tests (`spendingWaterfall.spec.ts`).
  - **Accordion preserved.** Expanding a Grouping emits a **header row** (which
    keeps the − collapse toggle and shows the group's net change at 40 % opacity)
    followed by its Category steps in place; because the category deltas sum to the
    group delta, the running total on either side is unchanged. Many open at once
    (`SvelteSet`), like the magnitude chart.
  - **Rendering** is a self-contained `SpendingBridge.svelte` — percentage-scaled
    off the model's running-total domain (no width measurement, resizes for free),
    Importance colour on the row's left border + a legend, hover tooltip with
    current / prior / change. Only reachable when the prior year has data (the
    `Bridge` toggle is disabled otherwise). 3 render tests.

**Known limitations (documented, not bugs).**

- **Disappeared spend is invisible in the table & chart.** The Change column and
  the side-by-side prior bar both hang off the _current_ report's rows, so a
  Grouping/Category that had spend last year but none this year has no row/bar to
  annotate. The Grand-Total row still reflects it. (The abandoned Bridge view
  surfaced it as a downward step — the one thing only that view did; if it's
  wanted again, build **diverging change bars**, not a waterfall. See
  [ADR-0004](../adr/0004-abandon-spending-bridge-waterfall-view.md).)
- **Whole-month only** (see the parity rule) — the current partial month is
  compared against the prior year's _full_ same month.

## Deferred (later slices)

- ~~Prior-period overlay line + year-over-year comparison~~ — **built ✅** (a table
  Change column + a prior-period bar marker; pending release), see
  [Year-over-year comparison](#year-over-year-comparison--table-columns--bar-marker-built-).
  A third **Bridge / waterfall** view was built and **abandoned as not intuitive**
  ([ADR-0004](../adr/0004-abandon-spending-bridge-waterfall-view.md)). Richer YoY
  views remain deferred: **cumulative pace line**, **diverging change bars**.
- ~~Historical-year expense upload~~ — **built ✅** (pending release), see section above.
- Arbitrary period / quarter selection (beyond a single calendar year).
- The multi-chart-type menu and any second chart type (trend, magnitude).
- Hierarchy tier CRUD — mostly built (assign + re-parent, and now **add/rename
  Groupings**, v0.67). **Importance-area CRUD is a permanent non-goal** — the 3
  seeded areas are fixed and will not change. Not built (but possible later):
  **Grouping delete** (empty groups are inert) and **Grouping reorder**
  (`sort_order`). See the Editable-hierarchy section above.
- Export (CSV / PDF).
- Promoting the report to the home page.

## Known limitations (document when building)

- **Refunds.** Refunds are represented as **negative `total_amount`** on a
  receipt (confirmed via `formatCurrency.spec.ts` and the export services). The
  report **keeps the sign**, so refunds net against spend — which is the correct
  behaviour for a spending total. (Note the CSV/PDF _exporters_ deliberately
  `abs()` refunds; the report does not.) One visible consequence: a Category or
  Grouping whose refunds exceed its spend in the window shows a **negative**
  total — informative, not a bug. No special handling needed in v1; documented
  here so the divergence from the exporters is intentional and searchable.
- **"Year to Date" label** reads oddly for a _completed past_ year (it is the
  full-year total). Relabel per-context when the multi-year slice lands. Not a
  v1 problem since v1 is current-year only.

Nearly all of it is built. Verified against the code, not just the doc's own checkmarks.

**Shipped:** v1 table, chart view, table-cell drill-down, hierarchy editor (assign, re-parent, add/rename Groupings), assign-on-create, historical-year import, and year-over-year (Change column + side-by-side prior-year bars). The Bridge/waterfall was built and removed — `grep` for `waterfall|Bridge` in `src/` returns nothing, matching [ADR-0004](docs/adr/0004-abandon-spending-bridge-waterfall-view.md).

**Genuinely left — six items:**

1. **Chart-bar drill-down.** The one real gap. Table cells link into `/expenses`; `SpendingChart.svelte` has no `href` or `goto` anywhere. The pure `buildSpendingDrilldownParams` already exists, so this is wiring, not design.
2. **Cumulative pace line** (option 3) — the deliberate home for the month/time story dropped from the bars.
3. **Diverging change bars** (option 4) — also the only remaining fix for "disappeared spend is invisible", since the Bridge that surfaced it is gone. The doc's colour constraint stands: red/green is taken by expense/refund.
4. **Quarter / arbitrary period selection** — no `quarter` anywhere in `src/`.
5. **Export (CSV/PDF).**
6. **Promoting the report to the home page.**

**Not left — permanent non-goals**, worth naming so they don't get re-planned: Importance-area CRUD (the 3 areas are fixed by product decision), Grouping delete and reorder (an empty Grouping is inert because zero-activity rows are suppressed), and the Bridge (do not rebuild).

**One limitation has quietly gone live.** The doc says the "Year to Date" label reads oddly for a completed past year, then dismisses it: *"Not a v1 problem since v1 is current-year only."* That premise expired when historical import shipped — the label is still hardcoded at `src/routes/spending/+page.svelte:384`, and a family that has imported 2024 now sees "Year to Date" over a full-year column. Small, but it's a live defect now rather than a deferred note.

**Two docs are stale about this.** The doc still says the YoY work is "pending release" — it went out around v0.612 (`c7b2dd3`), five versions ago. And `docs/product-backlog.md:16` is worse: it lists **"prior-period overlay + year-over-year"** as still open when it shipped, and describes hierarchy CRUD as "create/rename/delete/reorder Groupings + Importance areas" when create/rename are built, delete/reorder are deferred-as-pointless, and Importance-area CRUD is a settled non-goal. Read today, that line overstates what's left by a lot.

Want me to correct the backlog line and the doc's release status? The design doc itself should stay in `docs/plans/` — unlike the resize one, this genuinely isn't finished.
Correct it's status that is what confused me.

lines: ## Features

-- **Spending Report — remaining slices.** The report ships: table + chart views, cell drill-down, editable hierarchy, assign-on-create, and historical-expense import are all live. Still open, roughly in priority order: **chart-bar drill-down** (the same drill affordance the table cells have — carry the cell-link into `/expenses` from a bar/bracket click); **hierarchy tier CRUD** (create/rename/delete/reorder Groupings + Importance areas, with cascade-delete confirmations); **prior-period overlay + year-over-year** (unblocked now that historical years can be imported); quarter/period selection; multi-chart menu; export. See [Spending Report design](plans/2026-07-09-spending-report-design.md).

+- **Spending Report — remaining slices.** The report ships: table + chart views, cell drill-down, editable hierarchy (assign, re-parent, add & rename Groupings), assign-on-create, historical-expense import, **and year-over-year comparison** (table Change column + side-by-side prior-year bars) are all live. Still open, roughly in priority order: **chart-bar drill-down** (the same affordance the table cells have — carry the cell-link into `/expenses` from a bar/bracket click; `buildSpendingDrilldownParams` already exists); the two richer YoY views, a **cumulative pace line** and **diverging change bars** (the latter is also the only remaining way to surface spend that _disappeared_ vs last year); quarter/period selection; multi-chart menu; export. Also small and now live: the **"Year to Date" column heading is hardcoded**, so it reads wrong over an imported past year. **Not coming** — Importance-area CRUD (fixed at 3 areas, settled), Grouping delete/reorder, and the Bridge/waterfall ([ADR-0004](adr/0004-abandon-spending-bridge-waterfall-view.md)). See [Spending Report design](plans/2026-07-09-spending-report-design.md).

- **Receipt notes in the exports.** Deferred from [Receipt Notes](plans-done/2026-08-03-receipt-notes-design.md), which shipped without them. **CSV** is ~2 lines — one header entry plus one `escapeCSVField` call in `CSVExportService.buildRow` (`:79`); escaping already handles commas, quotes and newlines, and `parseExpenseImportCsv` ignores columns it does not need, so re-import is unaffected. The column appends after Category, so existing spreadsheet formulas on A–D are untouched. **PDF per-receipt page** is one line under the existing reference header (`PDFExportService.ts:470`, `:506`) — the page where you are already looking at the receipt itself. The PDF **summary table** was rejected rather than deferred: fixed column x-positions (`:49`) on an already-tight roll-up, for a detail field that does not belong in a spend summary.
- **Receipt image — rotate.** Rotate left and right anywhere a receipt is viewed.

- **Profile — manage emails.** Let users add/edit the email addresses associated with their account. This interacts with the unverified-alias security item below — verification is the fix, so design them together.

content.text:
Fixed. The status block was the problem — it was one dense paragraph that opened with "✅ Built", then buried the remaining work in a parenthetical at the end.

It now reads **🚧 Mostly built**, with three labelled parts:

- **Live** — one sentence listing every shipped slice.
- **Left** — the six items as a list, chart-bar drill-down first, plus the note that `buildSpendingDrilldownParams` already exists so it's wiring rather than design.
- **Will not be built** — Importance-area CRUD, Grouping delete/reorder, and the Bridge. Separated out explicitly because "deferred" and "decided against" were previously mixed together in the same sentence, which is a good way to have someone rebuild the waterfall.

**Four stale "pending release" claims** are gone from the body — the historical import and the YoY section both carried them, and both have been live for a while. I didn't assign version numbers to those slices: `4fad4cb` shipped as `0.69` while HEAD is `0.67`, so the numbering was reset at some point and any tag I inferred would be a guess.

**The "Year to Date" limitation now says its premise expired.** It had been dismissed as "not a v1 problem since v1 is current-year only" — true when written, false since historical import shipped. It names the hardcoded heading at `src/routes/spending/+page.svelte:384`.

**The backlog line got the same treatment.** It was listing **year-over-year as still open** when it's live, and describing hierarchy CRUD as including Importance areas — which is a permanent non-goal. Both corrected, with the not-coming items named so they don't cycle back in.

The doc stays in `docs/plans/` — it isn't done.
